News.title: Fury after millions of phones ring out with wildfire emergency alert leaving Brits fume alarm was ‘absolute abuse’
News.content:
BRITS have been left fuming after a blaring emergency alert suddenly ripped through millions of phones tonight, warning of the soaring risk of wildfires.

The government urged people to “not light anything that could spark a fire”, including barbecues, campfires and fireworks, as Britain battles another spell of scorching heat.



But the deafening siren accompanying the alert immediately sparked a backlash, with some questioning whether such an ear-splitting warning was necessary.

One furious Brit said: “@GOVUK absolute abuse of the Severe Alert system, which is now being turned off on my phone.



“You’ve totally undermined the purpose of the system. Send a text, for sure, but don’t abuse emergency broadcast systems to tell us about not using BBQs.

Another fumed: “The noise accompanying that emergency alert feels overkill.

“Lot of older people or those hiding phones for their safety possibly put at risk. Does it have to come with a loud noise?”

A third blasted the siren saying it sounded more like a warning to flee for your life than a reminder to put away the barbecue.

They wrote: “It’s for emergencies, so the noise seems reasonable. Whether it should have been used on this occasion is a different matter

One more commented: “The noise was giving ‘you have 10 minutes to evacuate your home’ not ‘put the BBQ away’.”



The blaring alert pinged phones across the country at around 7pm today, accompanied by a piercing siren designed to grab attention.

Brits were alerted even if their phone was put on silent, with the vibration lasting around ten seconds.

It warned: “Even a small flame can rapidly develop into a major wildfire placing lives, homes, businesses and emergency responders at risk.”

The alert added: “Recipients will also be urged to report any fire immediately by calling 999.”

It comes as wildfires and blazes have rattled the country in recent weeks.



Just yesterday, a total of 11 major fire incidents were reported in the past 24 hours in the West Midlands alone.

But residents of the UK were left almost hysterical at the lack of severity of the alert.

News.title: Millions of Brits’ phones ring out with emergency alert warning them not to start blazes due to wildfires risk
News.content:
MILLIONS of Brits have just received an emergency alert on their phones warning against the high risk of wildfires.

The government issued the alert warning people “not to light anything that could spark a fire, including barbecues, campfires, and fireworks” with the country in the middle of another heatwave.



The blaring alert pinged the phones of millions across the nation around 7pm today.

The alert has gone through even if a phone is set to silent, with the sound and vibration lasting about 10 seconds.



Accompanied by a siren sound, it warned that “even a small flame can rapidly develop into a major wildfire placing lives, homes, businesses and emergency responders at risk”.

The alert added: “Recipients will also be urged to report any fire immediately by calling 999.”



It comes as wildfires and blazes have swept the country in recent weeks.

Just yesterday, a total of 11 major fire incidents were reported in the past 24 hours in the West Midlands alone.



A total of 19 homes were completely destroyed and 18 others damaged as families forced to evacuate as the fire spread across Stourbridge, West Midlands, yesterday afternoon.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the request “came directly from Fire and Rescue Services”.

The Labour PM said: “This evening, an Emergency Alert has been sent to people across England and Wales as the wildfire risk remains very high.

“I was in Stourbridge today and saw first-hand the devastating impact these fires have had on people’s homes and lives.

“Our priority now is to keep everyone safe and prevent more fires from starting. During this period of extreme heat, I’m asking everyone to take extra care.



“Please do not light any fires in gardens, the countryside or other open spaces, including parks, moorland and wooded areas.

“Our firefighters and emergency responders are working around the clock in incredibly difficult conditions.

“We can all help them. Please take the Emergency Alert seriously and follow the guidance in place.”

The surge in fires came as the UK officially broke its 2026 record for the hottest day, with the mercury hitting 38.5C in Kew Gardens, London.

The fire in Stourbridge was fuelled by extreme heat and high winds and the 500-acre blaze quickly escalated into a major incident.



There were multiple wildfires reported across the Midlands yesterday, including also in Stoke-on-Trent, Birmingham, Warwickshire and Worcestershire – as well as others in Norfolk and Wales.

Louise Haigh, the First Secretary of State, said: “This is the most extensive use of the UK’s Emergency Alert system in response to an active incident, and reflects the seriousness with which the government is acting to safeguard people and property.

“During this period of extreme heat, we are asking people to take simple steps to limit the risk of further fires.

“The government will continue to provide every assistance to communities being impacted by these fires, including the deployment of 100 additional military personnel in major incident areas.”

The Emergency Alert system has been used before but the siren was part of a test when sounding out in September last year.



Phones vibrated and emitted a siren-like tone for up to 10 seconds.

The Government has also used the system to issue real warnings.

The last real use was on 8 January when there was a threat to life from high winds in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

In January 2025, during Storm Eowyn, the system warned people in Scotland and Northern Ireland about severe weather.

Approximately 3.5 million people across Wales and south-west England received an alert during Storm Darragh in December 2024.



In February 2024, a 500kg unexploded Second World War bomb found in a Plymouth back garden triggered a warning to some 50,000 phones.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Messages can be targeted to relatively small areas to pinpoint those at risk.

Some 15,000 phones were alerted during flooding in Cumbria in May 2024, and 10,000 received a warning during flooding in Leicestershire in January this year.

News.title: Shocking moment massive mudslide barrels down hill as torrential rain drowns town in huge floods and kills one
News.content:
THIS is the moment a powerful mudslide sends a deluge of water surging downhill in a huge flash flood that has killed one person.

The massive landslip was triggered by sudden flooding as heavy bursts of heavy rain hit China’s eastern Zhejiang Province on Friday.



At least three people are missing – though authorities fear there may be more – after the torrent of water hit in Changxing County near Shanghai around 6.20am.

Shocking footage captures the moment fast flowing waters spring across a road – felling trees and collapsing buildings.



Countless tree trunks rush with the flowing waters that hit the town.

Imagery from the aftermath shows cars submerged in the muddy waters, floating in the lake that now sits in the area.

People can be seen wading through the water-logged wreckage with levels reaching their chest.

Officials say rescue work was underway as emergency crews continue working in the affected area.



It comes as eastern and southern provinces of China continue to brace for more downpours and floods.

China is ⁠increasingly battling destructive weather as the emerging El Niño pattern boosts temperatures and fuels more ​frequent and intense typhoons.

More than one million people were evacuated from several provinces – including Zhejiang – in the east of the country last week as Typhoon Dolphin hit the area.



Huge landfalls ⁠were seen on on Sunday as a result of the extreme rain.

Many streets in Shanghai, the country’s second most populous city, were flooded, including in the main commercial centres.

In July natural disasters left 318 people dead or missing in China and caused direct economic ​losses of £6.28 billion (57.15 billion yuan), according to data released by ​the emergency management ministry.

In central China’s Henan Province, authorities were organising the ​evacuation of 781 ​people after a ⁠riverbank was breached late on Thursday in the city of Zhoukou.

Remnants of ​Typhoon Dolphin, combined with cold air and a monsoon ​trough, are ⁠expected to bring more heavy rain in eastern and southeastern China from Friday to Sunday.



A basin-wide major flood is ⁠expected in ​Lake Tai in the east, the country’s ​third-largest freshwater lake and the origin of a number of rivers, according to CCTV.

News.title: Where is Alejandra Mendoza now? The true story behind A Child of My Own on Netflix
News.content:
MAITE Alberdi’s new Netflix documentary A Child of My Own tells the story of one of the most unusual criminal cases in recent Mexican history.

It portrays the real life events and actions carried out by Eleonor Alejandra Marín Mendoza, who took desperate measures in order to enact her dream of being a mother.



How did Alejandra Mendoza end up in jail?

In 2008, Mendoza (known as Ale) was 25 years old and facing pressure from her loved ones to become a mother, having just suffered a series of miscarriages.

After her third loss, Mendoza was pushed to the limit and decided to fake a pregnancy by deliberately gaining weight, lying to her family and husband, Arturo, for months.



Across this time, she faked medical reports and went on maternity leave after attending an appointment with her husband where a doctor attempted to listen for the heartbeat of the “baby”.

When her “due date” came along in June 2009, she was arrested for stealing a newborn baby from a New Mexico hospital in an act of desperation, shocking the entire country.



Despite claiming she had permission from the mother of the infant, she and Arturo were ultimately convicted of kidnapping – although the latter claimed to know nothing about the act.

Arturo was eventually acquitted following his trial, having already served two years and six months in prison for initially being considered an accomplice to his wife.

“I was drawn into problems that got bigger and bigger,” says Ale in the documentary.

“And I started making decisions and taking actions which got more complicated, until there was no way out. No turning back.”



Where is Alejandra Mendoza now?

A Child of My Own was released on Netflix on Thursday, August 13 after making its world premiere at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival back in February.

The film has a runtime of just over an hour-and-a-half, with the story centring around the real-life crime committed by Eleonor Alejandra Marín Mendoza.

Directed by two-time Oscar nominated documentary filmmaker Maite Alberdi, her latest project is staged as a cinematic ‘docudrama’ for the first half of the film, with Ana Celeste portraying Mendoza.



It then structurally changes at the halfway mark, with the second half shifting to a more traditional documentary as it shows real life encounters of Mendoza being interviewed in a Mexican jail, whilst also presenting first-hand testimonies and court reports of the case.

Upon meeting her, director Alberdi said: “Alejandra wasn’t someone I would have imagined ending up in prison.

“I was struck by how extraordinary everything she told me was.”

Mendoza had to spend 13 years, three months, and 25 days in jail.

In the last few weeks of her sentence she completed the interview which is shown in the film.



She was released from prison in 2023, and currently lives as a free woman in Mexico.

She said: “During my thirteen years in prison, I have focused on accepting not being a mum.”

“Before, I think my desire to be a mum was more about pleasing others. What else is out there beyond being a mum?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But I finally realised there’s so much more to live for.”

The documentary shows that Mendoza and her husband Arturo reconciled and are now back together, after initially separating while she was serving time.

News.title: Can I still have a barbecue in my garden? The Government ban on disposable BBQs explained
News.content:
THE government has made the decision to temporarily BAN disposable barbecues due to the “significant risk” they present.

It comes after a series of wildfires across the UK – but what are the rules and safety recommendations around using a standard barbecue this summer?



Can I still have a BBQ in my garden?

The government order issued on Friday August 14 states: “The government considers that the supply and subsequent foreseeable use of disposable barbecues poses a significant risk to the public, and the environment, and therefore cannot be considered a safe product.

“They should not be made available for supply either in store or online at the current time.”



These guidelines refer specifically to barbecues that are domestic, single-use only, and not intended for re-filling or reuse.

They comprise of a fuel tray, grill grid and include charcoal fuel sufficient to provide the necessary cooking temperature for the duration of a single cooking session.



Retailers and distributors have been informed not to sell the products, with “criminal sanctions” put in place for those who don’t comply.

The government advises that the ban is set to remain in place until weather conditions change sufficiently to reduce the level of risk, and “will be withdrawn in consultation with relevant departments and agencies”.

There is currently no formal, nationwide guidance in place relating to permanent, non-disposable home barbecues designed for repeated use.

However, various councils and fire services around the country have issued guidance around using your barbecue safely.



What are the key barbecue safety tips?

Location

The first step in ensuring you have a safe barbecue is setting it up in an appropriate location.

As per the Norwich City Council, it should always be placed on a flat, stable level, ground, and never be placed directly onto dry grass, vegetation or a balcony of any kind.

Also remember to keep it well away from any sheds, fences, trees, plants and anything else that could a fire.

Finally, make sure to have safety equipment ready by your side, that being either a bucket of water, a bucket of sand or a garden hose.



Concentration

Another important factor in making sure you are in full control of your barbecue is to have maximum concentration.

To do so, make sure to never leave the barbecue unattended, even for just a small amount of time, while it’s still lit or hot.

Also be sure to keep children, pets, and any form of garden game well away from the cooking zone.

Finally, the London Fire Brigade states that the person manning the barbecue should never drink too much alcohol, as that can often slow reaction time and cause costly errors.



Finishing up…

Once the cooking is finished, wait until the barbecue has cooled down and make sure the embers and ashes have been fully extinguished.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

From that point, empty the ash onto bare soil, and as the Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service points out, remember to never to discard them straight into a dustbin.

And be aware that smouldering ashes can give off dangerous carbon monoxide fumes.

News.title: Brutal world of dolphin shows with tormented ‘self-harming’ animals crammed into tiny concrete tanks and kicked by kids
News.content:
COVERED in scars and visibly distressed, a bottlenose dolphin poses for photos with tourists before being forced to perform tricks to a cheering crowd.

Later, they’re returned to a tiny concrete tank, where loud music blares constantly. This is the brutal reality behind Europe’s dolphin shows, with unwitting Brit tourists paying to watch them.



It is estimated that more than 3,700 whales and dolphins are being held captive across 345 facilities in 56 countries around the world – many snatched from the wild for entertainment, with bottlenose dolphins the most commonly held species.

Confined to tiny tanks, the animals can become so distressed that they self-harm – including slamming their heads against their enclosures, teeth grinding and refusing to eat – with animal rights campaigners describing their existence as a “living death”.

While the UK’s last Dolphinarium closed its doors in March 1993 and Canada, Chile, India and Costa Rica also banning dolphin shows, many European countries still allow them – and continue to flog tickets to the public, including Brits.



Scores of celebs, including Kim Kardashian, Kimberley Walsh and Wayne and Coleen Rooney, have also faced criticism for paying to swim or pose with dolphins on luxury trips.

PETA’s Vice President of Programmes Elisa Allen says: “These bright, complex, ocean-going mammals experience living death in tiny cement boxes and, unlike the tourists whose money keeps these attractions running, they never get to leave.

“Instead of exploring vast stretches of ocean, caring for their young, forming lifelong bonds, and conversing with each other, captive dolphins are forced to perform tawdry tricks and subjected to noise, stress and unwanted human handling.

“PETA urges everyone to keep their money in their pockets or risk keeping these pits of animal misery afloat.”

In the wild, dolphins can roam freely in territories spanning more than 100km, but in captivity, they are often confined to tanks of less than 5,000 square feet.



According to PETA, the result can lead to severe mental distress, with dolphins displaying repetitive behaviours, such as head bobbing and pacing.

In May, horrifying drone footage was shared of six dolphins at The Hyatt Ziva Cancún resort, where the former swimming pool is rented to dolphin experience company, Delphinus.

The dolphins were seen floating listlessly, and swimming in circles.



While Mexico is one country to ban dolphin shows, due to a 18-month legal transition phase which ends later this year, dolphins are still being held captive.

“These dolphins are in shallow tanks, have no escape, no shade, suffer from a constant barrage of disco music, and then at night a laser show keeps them awake,” says Marketa Schusterova, co-founder of animal rights group TideBreaker, who captured the footage.

“They are not medically looked after well, appear thin, have damage and scars on their bodies, and they are clearly distressed.”

Responding to the claims, a spokesperson for Hyatt Ziva Cancún previously said a third party Delphinus was responsible for the creatures, saying: “We understand the concerns raised regarding the dolphins at the resort.

“Delphinus is an organisation accredited by Mexican authorities and international agencies and is responsible for the care of the dolphins, including support from trained animal care and veterinary professionals.”



Palmitos Park in Gran Canaria, which has six male dolphins, has also come under fire from tourists who claim they witnessed trainers dragging the mammals and allowing children to kick them.

One visitor said: “The dolphins were in the pools with the tiniest amount of space to roam free and in the show they looked uncomfortable.”

Another said: “The dolphins were made to take pictures with the public for up to 40 mins before the show, the trainers towards the end were dragging the dolphins by their mouths to get them into position, one kid actually kicked the dolphin twice.”

Another park using the animals for entertainment is Loro Parque, Tenerife, which advertises trick shows with their dolphins Pacina, Luna, Ilse, Clara, Achille, Ulisse and Ebu.

With 2.7million Brits visiting Tenerife each year, many are likely to visit the park, probably not knowing the true scale of alleged cruelty behind the shows.



In 2023, The Dolphin Project publicly criticised the way the 33-acre wildlife park and zoo treated and paraded its aquatic mammals in front of an 1,800-capacity theatre.



The performances were said to include dolphins jumping over poles, spinning on platforms and balancing upside down in the water while waving their tail flukes at the audience.

In one shocking stunt, trainers would even use the dolphins as ‘ride-on toys’, which PETA has warned can cause serious harm and damage to the creatures, including impairing their hearing.

Dolphin encounters are not just popular with tourists – celebrities have also helped give the controversial attractions a glossy image by posing for pictures and swimming alongside the animals.

Reality TV star Sam Faiers found herself at the centre of a social media storm some time ago, after posting pictures of herself and her family taking part in a Dolphins Emotions swim experience at the controversial Zoomarine in Guia, Portugal in 2016.

The park had faced animal welfare allegations, including claims that dolphins were made to tow a small boat carrying children around the pool and were used as selfie props, with visitors able to kiss, hug and stroke them.



Speaking at the time, Sam defended the experience, saying: “To me they were being well looked after and fed, they had the biggest swimming pool to swim in.”

However, Zoomarine has since appeared on World Animal Protection’s list of 12 zoos globally to avoid.

The £950million Atlantis, The Palm on Dubai’s glitzy Palm Jumeirah is another celebrity hotspot for dolphin encounters.

When the mega-resort opened its doors in 2008, it pulled in a glittering crowd of celebs and royals, including Oprah Winfrey and The Duchess of York, but its dolphins soon became the centre of a storm over animals being used for entertainment.

Danny Groves from Whale and Dolphin Conservation, says: “There is no ethical reason in today’s world to keep dolphins and whales imprisoned in a concrete tank for their entire, shortened lives where they are forced to perform tricks to entertain us.



“What people who go to these shows often do not realise is the cruelty that their ticket money helps to perpetuate.”

And it appears attitudes are changing towards using dolphins as tourist attractions.

For example, UK holiday firms Jet2 and Easyjet have ended ticket sales to marine parks and other attractions offering dolphin experiences – while TUI has come under fire for not doing the same.

News.title: Tate brothers ‘drinking dirty brown shower water’ and are woken by ‘demonic roar’ of inmates in hellhole prison
News.content:
ANDREW and Tristan have complained about being held in a hellhole jail with “brown and filthy” shower water, where the sounds of “demonic roars” wake them up every night.

Andrew, 39, and brother Tristan, 38, have been locked up since their arrest at a bare-knuckle boxing event in Miami on July 18.



The brothers have been charged with rape, sex trafficking and offences related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

They are now being held in Florida’s Miami Federal Detention Center, where their lawyers claim they are suffering in the harsh conditions.



Self-described misogynist Andrew called his Special Housing Unit (SHU) “punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates“.

The dual US-UK citizen claimed he had been forced to drink unclean water that made him sick.

His only water source is a shower and a “brown and filthy faucet” which has left him suffering “persistent stomach problems”, he claims.

The jail has faced cooling and water problems and a clash between inmates and staff in recent months, according to the US Bureau of Prisons.

It comes as court documents revealed that the brothers held several passports under different aliases – including one name borrowed from a Bond villain.

Andrew said he had been woken up in the middle of the night by other prisoners yelling death threats and had heard a “demonic roar” from a neighbouring cell.



He also claimed he was staying in “the worst possible conditions the US gov provides to terrorists and psychopaths”, adding that the inmate in the neighbouring cell was a “cannibal who screams throughout the night”.

In another message on X, Andrew complained he had “no commissary. No visits. No contact with the outside world.”

He ranted: “I am an innocent until proven guilty extradition detainee. I’m wanted by a foreign state. I am an American citizen. WHY AM I HERE?”



Their lawyers claimed they had not been let out of their cells at all for 11 of their first 15 days in the jail.

Insiders told The Sun the conditions were a “disgrace”.

Last year, a report said inmates were forced to kneel and eat “like dogs”, with their hands shackled and food on chairs in front of them.

Toilets bubbling over with waste, crumbling infrastructure and an extreme use of force were also alleged by inmates’ families.

And as downtown Miami faces extreme heat, climbing above 30C, detainees say they have been left without air conditioning.



The facility has been blighted by AC issues for years, according to a 2020 report.

Inmates say they strip to their underwear amid the sweltering conditions and sweat through their sheets at night.

The brothers are fighting extradition to the UK, where they face a total of 59 criminal charges, including rape, sex trafficking and offenses related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Allegations against them include having sex with a minor, trafficking minors, running an organised crime operation and money laundering.

British prosecutors said new charges were fast-tracked after authorities investigated claims made by another four victims.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrew and Tristan both deny the charges and say they have done no wrongdoing.

A prison spokesperson told The Sun that inmates generally have access to commissary services, recreation, phone calls, social visits and legal counsel.

News.title: Woke plan to BAN white people from public pool sparks outrage and claims of ‘segregation’
News.content:
POOL FURY Woke plan to BAN white people from public pool sparks outrage and claims of ‘segregation’

A WOKE plan to ban white swimmers from a public pool in Berlin has sparked outrage and claims of segregation.

The Volksbühne theatre was given £255,000 of taxpayers’ money to open a “people’s swimming pool” that was supposed to be “open for all who are seeking to cool down in the increasingly hot Berlin summers”.



But the theatre advertised a six-hour event on Friday, August 14, when the 80ft open-air pop-up would be open “exclusively to black communities”.

The event, organised in partnership with the anti-discrimination group Each One Teach One, was due to shut the pool to the wider public from noon until 6pm.



Visitors were also asked to respect “this collective self-designation and the spaces associated with it”.

The decision sparked political backlash, with critics accusing organisers of turning a publicly funded facility into a racially divided space.

Stefan Evers, Berlin’s finance minister and Christian Democrat candidate for mayor, said: “I don’t believe in dividing people by skin colour.”

He added: “I understood the ‘People’s Swimming Pool’ as a swimming pool for everyone.”

Christoph Meyer, the centre-right Free Democratic Party candidate, also blasted the move.

He said: “Public spaces must bring society together, not segregate people based on skin colour.”



The event has now been cancelled, after the theatre complained it had become the “target of right-wing and racist incitement”.

Each One Teach One said it had received threatening and racist emails.

It added that could no longer guarantee the “physical and psychological safety” of the young people the event was intended for.



The theatre’s director, Matthias Lilienthal, has said he intends to rebook the event and will appear at the pool to discuss the controversy with members of the public.

The temporary pool, installed outside the city centre, is due to remain in place for eight weeks and is free for all guests.

The €300,000 (£256,000) project can accommodate just 46 swimmers at a time, with organisers estimating around 20,000 visitors during its run.

Lilienthal has said he hoped to give Berliners somewhere to swim as the city’s pool facilities face mounting pressure.

He told German broadcaster ZDF: “Half of the indoor and outdoor pools are closed, so we thought we’d help out Governing Mayor Kai Wegner.”



“The Volksbuhne considers even something as simple as two people splashing each other to be a theatrical event.”

The controversy comes during a sweltering summer in Germany, where extreme heat has placed further pressure on public swimming facilities.

Swimming pools have also increasingly become flashpoints for culture wars.

Last week, a swimming spot in Halle faced criticism after bathers were reportedly told they had to speak fluent German or risk being refused entry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pool said the rule was intended to help keep swimmers safe and ensure they could understand instructions.



Berlin’s swimming pools also introduced ID requirements in 2025 after a string of punch-ups and sexual harassment during hot summer days.

News.title: Millions startled by blaring emergency alert warning of 'very high' wildfire risk
News.content:
Millions startled by blaring emergency alert warning of 'very high' wildfire risk

The unexpected siren-like warning sounded on phones at 7pm, prompting startled reactions online as people were urged to avoid anything that could spark a wildfire

View 4 Images The government emergency alertis seen on a mobile phone today (Image: Jeff Moore)

Brits were left shocked after millions across England and Wales were sent a blaring Government emergency alert tonight with a stark warning.

‌



Phones sounded with the siren-like warning from around 7pm on Friday 14, with residents, and visitors urged not to do anything that could spark a blaze.

‌



The alert warned against disposable barbecues, fire pits, garden incinerators and fireworks, adding: “Even a small flame can rapidly develop into a major wildfire placing lives, homes, businesses and emergency responders at risk.”

‌



People were also told to follow official updates and call 999 immediately if they spot signs of a fire. It comes as firefighters continue to tackle blazes across the country following weeks of exceptionally hot and dry weather, with ministers stepping up efforts to prevent further fires with a disposable barbecue ban.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham also urged people to take “the greatest of care” as the country heads into the weekend (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

First Secretary Louise Haigh said: “In response to the continued risk proposed by wildfires, the government has taken the decision to issue an Emergency Alert to England and Wales. This is the most extensive use of the UK’s Emergency Alert system in response to an active incident, and reflects the seriousness with which the government is acting to safeguard people and property

‌



“During this period of extreme heat, we are asking people to take simple steps to limit the risk of further fires. By following the safety guidance, everyone can play their part in protecting local communities and supporting our frontline services who are working around the clock to keep people safe.

“The government will continue to provide every assistance to communities being impacted by these fires, including the deployment of 100 additional military personnel in major incident areas.”

The warning follows a temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues, which the Government said posed a “significant risk to the public” in the current conditions. Guidance states they should not currently be supplied either in shops or online, with the restriction remaining under review as weather conditions change.

‌



View 4 Images A wildfire warning was sent today (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Andy Burnham also urged people to take the greatest of care as the country heads into the weekend, warning against lighting anything outdoors. He tweeted: "This evening, an Emergency Alert has been sent to people across England and Wales as the wildfire risk remains very high. The request came directly from Fire and Rescue Services. I was in Stourbridge today and saw first-hand the devastating impact these fires have had on people’s homes and lives.

" Our priority now is to keep everyone safe and prevent more fires from starting. During this period of extreme heat, I’m asking everyone to take extra care. Please do not light any fires in gardens, the countryside or other open spaces, including parks, moorland and wooded areas. Our firefighters and emergency responders are working around the clock in incredibly difficult conditions. We can all help them. Please take the Emergency Alert seriously and follow the guidance in place."

‌



View 4 Images Fire crews continue to work at the scene near the burnt out remains of homes following a huge fire in Stourbridge (Image: Getty Images)

Mr Burnham, who has previously dealt with wildfires in Greater Manchester, said the scale of the destruction had shocked him. He said: “I’ve never seen anything like it. I mean, I dealt with wildfires in Greater Manchester, but nothing on this scale. I’ve never seen scenes like this in Britain, where you just see a whole house gutted, smouldering.”

The sudden warning quickly sparked reaction online, with some people admitting the loud alarm had caught them off guard.

‌



One X user said: “now why the hell did no one say we were getting an emergency alert. thought the f**king world was ending the way i just heard the entire street’s phones blaring from my garden”

Another said: “this alert scared me so bad my heart rate spiked to like 190 and I passed out on my kitchen floor i need my propranolol”

One user in Wales also complained about the language used in the message, writing: “Why would they send an emergency alert with no English translation at all???? This is not practical at all???? Not every Welsh person is fluent????”

Article continues below

The Emergency Alerts system was launched in April 2023 and allows warnings to be sent directly to compatible mobile phones where there is a danger to life. It has previously been used during major incidents including Storm Éowyn in January 2025, when around 4.5million people across Scotland and Northern Ireland received an urgent warning over extreme weather.

News.title: Netanyahu trashed by British Jews for calling UK ‘the Islamic Republic of Britain’
News.content:
Netanyahu trashed by British Jews for calling UK ‘the Islamic Republic of Britain’

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sparked backlash after calling the UK the “Islamic Republic of Britain” during a podcast appearance.

View Image Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called the UK the “Islamic Republic of Britain” in (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called the UK the “Islamic Republic of Britain” in a podcast interview that has sparked widespread criticism.

‌



The Israeli leader made the comments during an appearance on the Melech Blitzer Haim podcast on Thursday while discussing British media coverage of Israel.

‌



During the podcast, Netanyahu praised British writer Randolph Churchill, the son of former prime minister Winston Churchill, for what he described as his “positive” coverage of Israel during the 1967 Six-Day War.

‌



According to translated comments published by Israeli media, he then said: “Go find that in Britain today, which you could call the Islamic Republic of Britain.”

Netanyahu later appeared to echo previous comments made by JD Vance about Britain becoming the first “truly Islamist country” to get a nuclear weapon.

He said: “Someone said the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons will be the Islamic Republic of Britain.

‌



“We are making sure there won’t be another one here, in Iran.”

His comments were branded “blatant Islamophobia” by Gavin Barwell, who previously served as Downing Street chief of staff to Theresa May.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Writing on X, Mr Barwell added: “Let’s hope everyone will now shed the pretence some still cling to that this man is any friend of Britain.”

A British and Irish Jewish group also criticised Netanyahu’s comments, saying the Israeli prime minister “does not speak for British Jews”.

The Movement for Progressive Judaism added: “At a time when antisemitism, anti-Muslim hatred and social division are causing real fear across our country, language of this kind is dangerous and irresponsible.

‌



“Prime Minister Netanyahu does not speak for British Jews. His words do not represent us.”

The comments come amid strained relations between the British and Israeli governments.

The UK has paused negotiations on a new free trade agreement with Israel and suspended some arms export licences. Britain has also imposed sanctions on Israeli cabinet ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

‌



Last year, the UK formally recognised the State of Palestine alongside countries including Canada and Australia.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently apologised for Labour’s initial response to Israel’s actions in Gaza, saying the party had been too slow to call for a ceasefire.

He said: “That is why we need to do more, which includes looking at further sanctions on those involved in the violence in Gaza but also looking at measures to ban trading goods with illegal settlements.

Article continues below

“We’ve got to do more to put pressure on the Israeli government.”

News.title: Boris Johnson is transformed from disheveled scruff to man from Matalan in startling new holiday snaps
News.content:
Boris Johnson is transformed from disheveled scruff to man from Matalan in startling new holiday snaps

Over the years, I've looked at topless pictures of Boris Johnson more than I would like. And this new set of Instagram pics is different in one important respect. He looks .... kind of alright

View 4 Images Boris looks...kind of alright in the latest set of photos (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Trim, groomed and well-dressed are not usually words you'd associate with Boris Johnson holiday snaps.

‌



Disheveled, scruffy and ill-fitting were more commonly found in newspaper tales about Johnson's regular Grecian getaways. So when images of the Johnsons holidaying on an island landed on wife Carrie's Instagram yesterday (FRI), they raised a few eyebrows.

‌



Carrie, is typically goddess-esque in the photoset. No change there. Although there is one snap where she's leaning so far back on a stool I feared for the integrity of her spine. If that's a natural sitting position for her, she may wish to consider becoming acquainted with a chiropractor.

‌



View 4 Images Carrie Johnson just sitting on a stool normally, as one does (Image: INSTAGRAM)

But Boris is the real surprise, because he looks .... alright. I'd hesitate to use the low-effort "Boris looks unrecognisable" trope, but it's not far off. He's had a haircut and a shave, although that line of fluff along his lower jaw continues to stubbornly avoid his razor. He's not wearing his usual holiday uniform of noisy board shorts paired with, for some reason, an un-ironed dress shirt. (Never ironed, always tucked in to the shorts.) Instead he's paired the deafening shorts with tasteful tee shirts. Or, in several of the snaps, with nothing at all. And, I wouldn't want to lead readers to think I've developed a thirst for Britain's second worst Prime Minister, but I say again, he looks ... alright.

‌



View 4 Images The camera angles, they are flattering (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Over the years, I've looked at pictures of Boris Johnson with his top off more than I would like. And be they long-lenses, selfies and those unfortunate snaps of him trying out boogie boarding, presumably for the first time, none of them showed him in a particularly flattering light. Until now. He's all shoulder and arms, barely an unsightly curve or flap in sight. I have no idea if it's diet, exercise, jabs or flattering camera angles - though I suspect it's the latter, or he'd bored everyone with it in a deceptively wordy column - but something's working for him. Of course, none of this matters. Our coverage of Boris Johnson's lazy days on sun-drenched beaches during the Number 10 years usually focused on which billionaire owned said stretch of sandy coastline, or which national crisis he was neglecting in order to sup Mythos outside a faux rustic villa.

View 4 Images He's all shoulder and arm these days (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Article continues below

There's always been a theory that Johnson's cuddly scruffbag image was carefully curated. And I've personally seen him deliberately messing up his hair moments before walking out to give a speech, so as to bolster his practiced bumbling. But something - maybe it was the dress shirts on the beach - always returned me to the conclusion that he is naturally lacking in care for his appearance. This has, apparently changed. He's putting in the effort - at least for the purposes of Carriegram.

But Boris should bear in mind that if he ever attempted to parlay this new Man from Matalan image as a soft soap route back into British public life, he would barely make it past customs before being chased back onto the plane by families from around Britain still furious that he presided over Partygate while they held weddings and funerals on zoom.

News.title: Wickford train derailment - live: Greater Anglia train comes off tracks in Essex
News.content:
A Greater Anglia train has derailed near Wickford in Essex - the second train to derail in the UK within 24 hours - with services cancelled between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria

Wickford train derailment - live: Greater Anglia train comes off tracks in Essex

A Greater Anglia train carrying 62 passengers has derailed close to Wickford in Essex, sparking a major emergency response.

The incident is understood to have happened between Wickford and Rayleigh at around 2.21pm, with trains cancelled between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria.

National Rail said "major disruption" is expected on the rail network until at least 6pm. Air ambulances have been scrambled, although there are no reports of injuries thus far. People nearby reported feeling their buildings shake.

It comes after a major incident was declared by British Transport Police when three carriages derailed and trapped passengers on board a Southern train near Lewes on Thursday afternoon.

Were you on the derailed train in Essex this afternoon? Email livenews@reachplc.com.

News.title: Billionaire Mike Ashley's takeover of Harvey Nichols means it 'won't look like the same business'
News.content:
He is the tracksuit tycoon who made a staggering fortune with his 'stack-em-high, sell-em-cheap' tactics that turned Sports Direct into a retail powerhouse.

Now self-made billionaire Mike Ashley has pulled off his most unexpected deal yet by snapping-up posh department store Harvey Nichols.

From the outside, there is vast different between the bargain bins at Sports Direct and Harvey Nichols’ luxury flagship store in London’s swanky Knightsbridge. In its 1990s heyday, fans included Princess Diana and other ‘Sloane Rangers’. It was name-checked heavily in the TV comedy Absolutely Fabulous, starring Joanna Lumley and Jennifer Saunders.

But the more you examine the deal, the more it carries the hallmarks of others clinched by Ashley, 61, namely a loss-making retailer with a strong brand that has fallen on hard times bought for a song.

‌



Which begs the question, what will Mr Ashley’s Frasers empire now do with Harvey Nichols, which also has stores in Edinburgh, Leeds, Birmingham, Manchester and Bristol?

View 5 Images Future of famous department store Harvey Nichols unclear after takeover by Frasers

The message from Frasers chief executive Michael Murray, who is Ashley’s son-in-law, was ominous when he warned: “We are prepared to make those decisions, even if it means a smaller business in the near term.”

Independent retail analyst Richard Hyman said Ashley’s reported £40million purchase is likely to have included the huge incentive of the stock - acres of big brand clothing and the like - that came with it.

‌



“The one thing you can say for sure is that Harvey Nichols won’t look like the same business it does now,” he said. “We really don’t know what he will do but Mike Ashley isn’t about saving the high street, and that can’t be done by one person anyway.

“However, it has been clear in recent years that Frasers has been more focused on aspirational retail brands.”

Those include its Flannels high street chain, which sells designer gear, as well as Jack Wills, House of Fraser and Savile Row tailor Gieves & Hawkes, three of the many distressed brands Ashley has added to his empire.

View 5 Images Mike Ashley's empire is based on the success of sports chain Sports Direct (Image: Getty Images)

‌



His addition of Harvey Nichols comes as the wider luxury market is having a tough time.

Ashley and his management are likely to use the deal to turn the screw on store landlords to slash the chain’s rent costs.

The other intriguing factor is the role of Michael Murray, the former nightclub promoter from Doncaster who met Ashley’s daughter Anna while on holiday in 2011.

The son of a property developer, Murray, still aged just 36, is the Frasers Group’s chief executive, and seen as one of the architects of its move upmarket. Before taking over from his father-in-law, he was the group’s “head of elevation”.

‌



Brash businessman Ashley has concedes that his fitness-obsessed son-in-law - who he describes as “the pretty boy” - is more acceptable to luxury brands than a man who once described himself as “a power drinker”. “I’m Marmite - I’m not everyone’s cup of tea,” said Ashley.

Ashley has insisted that Murray makes the final call on investments but the tycoon - worth £3.4billion - still holds huge sway and owns nearly three quarters of the group.

And Ashley was clearly heavily involved in buying Harvey Nichols, claiming in the run-up to the deal it was in a “death spiral” and turning around business would be a “huge challenge”.

He also told the FT beforehand that, were he to succeed, he would be inclined to keep the retailer’s flagship store in Knightsbridge and its store in Edinburgh trading under the Harvey Nichols brand. However, he said some of its other stores would be rebranded as either House of Fraser or Flannels.

‌



Snapping-up such a high class retailer as Harvey Nichols - even given its battles in recent years - marks another milestone for Mr Ashley, who opened his first shop in 1982 in Maidenhead, Berks, with a £10,000 loan from his parents Keith and Barbara.

However, his maverick business style has always raised eyebrows, not least in the City where the group’s track record on corporate governance has been criticised in the past. His ownership of Newcastle United also proved highly controversial.

All eyes will now be on what his plans are for the chain, and the future of its 1,000 strong workforce.

View 5 Images Mike Ashley gives media a tour of the Sports Direct warehouse at Shirebrook, Derbyshire (Image: GETTY )

‌



Graham Hiscott's view

Meeting Mike Ashley was - and remains - one of the more bizarre interviews in my career.

It was 2016 and the maverick billionaire, who until then had remained fiercely private, was giving me a tour of Sports Direct’s vast Shirebrook warehouse in Derbyshire to try to counter claims staff endured “gulag” like conditions.

Here was a man - more a enigma - who had helped shape Britain’s high street in recent years, yet never gave interviews, despite fascinating snippets about unorthodox business dealings.

Wearing suit, black and white tie - he still owned Newcastle United then - and hi-vis, he certainly wasn’t lost for words. And in an industry where big bosses are media trained not to call a spade a spade, Ashley was a godsend for any journalist. From then Labour leader Ed Miliband who had who singled out what he said were Sports Direct’s “Victorian” working conditions: “I would love to get him in a boxing ring with a pair of gloves on and box his ears, that’s what I would like to do”, to his frank admission that he regretted owning Newcastle United.

‌



View 5 Images Sports Direct founder Mike Ashley empties his pockets of £50 bank notes during a mock search at the Sports Direct headquarters in Shirebrook, Derbyshire (Image: PA)

Six months later I was next to Ashley when in front of other journalists at Shirebrook, he pulled a huge wad of £50 notes form his pocket. Ashley joked: “I’ve been to the casino.”

It was around the same time as court case when it emerged Ashley vomited into a fireplace after downing 12 pints during a meeting in a pub. He would also allegedly “have a nap” under the table if he was bored during business talks, a banker suing him claimed.

It is perhaps not surprising that, after this brief spell in the public eye, Ashley opted to largely shun outings in front of the camera. However, through this time, and researching how Ashley created his empire, I was able to get a glimpse into what made him tick.

‌



And it clear that he loves the thrill of the chase when it comes to business, the buzz of the deal, a gambler, but only on his terms. His brash exterior belies a retail mastermind and cut-throat adversary.

It would be easy to think that buying upmarket Harvey Nichols is somehow his attempt to buy his way into the establishment. Ashley is no rags-to-riches story, but he has spent his career operating on the sidelines when it comes to the business elite. However, I think that’s just where he likes to be, snapping-up Harvey Nichols is just another transaction that made cold business sense.

News.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to shooting healthcare CEO: "I shot Mr Thompson and he died"
News.content:
Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to shooting healthcare CEO: "I shot Mr Thompson and he died"

Luigi Mangione was charged with ambushing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside a New York hotel as he walked to an annual investor conference

View 7 Images Mangione entered his plea at a federal court (Image: David Dee Delgado/UPI/Shutterstock)

Luigi Mangione has pleaded guilty over the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

‌



The 28-year-old was charged with ambushing Thompson, 50, outside a New York City hotel on December 4, 2024, as the insurance executive walked to an annual investor conference.

‌



Mangione entered his plea at a federal court with the hearing having been hastily requested by prosecutors and defence lawyers earlier this week.

‌



He said he learned that UnitedHealthcare would be holding an investor conference in New York, he researched online and used a 3D printer to make part of a gun. "I travelled to New York with the intent to shoot Brian Thompson," he said. "I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan and he died.

“I understood that my actions would place him in fear of death or bodily injury. I knew what I was doing was illegal.”

View 7 Images Mangione is accused of ambushing Thompson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Mangione told the court in a prepared statement of having suffered for a long time with back pain. When he admitted to killing the CEO of UnitedHealthcare, his widow Paulette Thompson began to sob and was comforted by two women next to her.

The defendant replied "guilty" when US District Judge Margaret Garnett asked how he pleaded to the two counts in the indictment. The judge said she would enter his plea.

In a news conference afterwards his lawyer Karen Friedman Agnifilo said he accepted “full responsibility for the death of Brian Thompson” with his guilty plea.

‌



She added: “As Luigi explained in court today, he endured years of severe, debilitating pain following a broken back while struggling to navigate our healthcare and health insurance systems.

View 7 Images UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson was killed in a attack (Image: AP)

"Like the thousands of people who have reached out since this tragedy to share their own experiences, he believed that the system had failed him and destroyed his life."

‌



The family of Mr Thompson said in a statement that today’s guilty plea “marks an important step toward justice for Brian and for our family.”

The statement continued: “While nothing will ease the pain of losing him, we are grateful that the federal justice system has held the person responsible for this heinous act accountable. Now we look to the court to ensure the sentencing reflects the severity of this crime.”

View 7 Images The victim's widow Paulette Thompson pictured outside court (Image: AP Photo/Ryan Murphy)

‌



A trial on state murder charges is scheduled to start next month and it is unclear whether that will go forward after Mangione pleaded guilty in the federal case. Mangione faces two federal charges that he stalked Thompson to cause his death which he has now pleaded guilty to.

Mangione's defence team has requested for the state charges to be dropped, said his lawyer Ms Friedman Agnifilo. Both the federal and state cases could lead to a life prison sentence while a federal judge earlier this year tossed out additional charges that could have exposed Mangione to a potential death penalty.

View 7 Images Members of Mr Thompson's family leaving court (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ms Friedman Agnifilo claimed that her client had been "unfairly" treated including with attempts to punish him twice.

“Mr Mangione has been unfairly treated since the outset in every way and has successfully fought off terrorism charges and the death penalty, while also fighting — at the same time — two simultaneous prosecutions in two jurisdictions, who are trying to punish him twice for the exact conduct,” she said.

“He’s been treated differently from every other defendant charged with this offense in New York.”

‌



After today's court hearing, Jamie McDonald, US attorney for the Southern District in New York, called the killing of Mr Thompson a "heinous act" which was "deliberate, calculated and premeditated".

And he hit back at supporters of Mangione saying: "There can be no celebrity in assassination, any person who celebrates, encourages or excuses actions like these is fundamentally wrong. Mangione attempted to send a public message through violence, but the message that emerges today is very different."

View 7 Images (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



While he also denied that there had been any plea bargaining. "he pled guilty to all pending counts in the indictment," he said. "There are no accommodations or concessions, and we are free to seek the maximum penalty under the law."

Mangione had complained about the prospect of two trials, telling a judge in February: "It's the same trial twice. One plus one is two. Double jeopardy by any common sense definition."

Under New York law, a state prosecution could potentially be barred if the federal case is resolved first. The state's double jeopardy protections kick in if a jury has been sworn in a prior prosecution, such as a federal case, or if that prosecution ends in a guilty plea. Mangione's cases involve different charges arising from the same course of conduct.

‌



In a letter last month, state prosecutors objected to the possibility of a guilty plea in the federal case wiping out the state case.

Judge Garnett in previously delivered some setbacks to the defence, including ruling in January that prosecutors could use items collected from Mangione's backpack during his arrest as evidence against him.

View 7 Images CCTV captured the moment Brian Thompson was shot outside a Manhattan hotel (Image: AP)

‌



They included a 3D-printed pistol that investigators said matched the one used to kill Thompson and a notebook in which authorities say Mangione described his intent to kill an insurance executive.

In June, Mangione's lawyers said they would pursue a psychiatric defence in the state case but reversed course a day later. The defence, involving claims that he was suffering from extreme emotional disturbance at the time of the killing, isn't allowed in federal court.

Surveillance video of the killing showed a masked gunman shooting Thompson from behind. Police say "delay," "deny" and "depose" were written on the ammunition, mimicking a phrase used to describe how insurers avoid paying claims.

Article continues below

Mangione, a University of Pennsylvania graduate from a wealthy Maryland family, was arrested five days later at a McDonald's in Altoona, Pennsylvania, about 230 miles west of Manhattan. He has become a cause celebre for some people upset with the health insurance industry.

News.title: Dark history behind Punch & Judy shows and why puppet has pointy chin
News.content:
Dark history behind Punch & Judy shows and why puppet has pointy chin

Iconic and utterly baffling in equal measure, there's something nostalgic about a Punch and Judy show. But did you know there's a reason Mr Punch looks the way he does?

View Image Punch and Judy shows have been a fixture of days at the seaside, village fetes, and country shows for hundreds of years (stock image) (Image: Staines & Chertsey Titles)

Is there anything more quintessentially British than a Punch and Judy show? A fixture of village shows, days at the seaside, and summer fetes, it's the sort of thing that leaves foreign visitors utterly baffled.

‌



The instantly-recognisable Mr Punch, with his big red nose, pointy chin, and wide smile, dates back around 350 years, with the first record of a marionette show featuring the character recorded by diarist Samuel Pepys in 1662. The shows quickly became a fixture in Britain, with Punch becoming something of a celebrity, according to the Victoria and Albert Museum.

‌



Joined by his long-suffering wife Joan - later renamed Judy - Punch was so popular that when a puppet show staged at London's Haymarket Theatre in 1773 did not feature the character, audiences reportedly rioted and tore up the benches. But did you know there's a dark reason for Punch's appearance?

‌



His big hooked nose and pointy chin aren't just for comedic effect - they actually suggest the highly-strung character is suffering from an unfortunate medical condition. Annabel Port runs The Other British Museum, which documents everyday items which symbolise the country, and explained in a video on Instagram.

"It's been said there's a reason for Punch's bad temper and prominent nose and chin," she said. "It was a caricature of the hormonal disorder acromegaly.

"I feel bad laughing now. Actually I'm not sure I ever have."

‌



People in the comments were amazed by the information. One said: "I always thought the reddened features were supposed to mean he was drunk."

Another agreed, saying: "I always thought he was a drunk. He wanted some sausages but his wife said no. Hence the violent response. Not quite sure where the crocodile originated in the story but it wanted the sausages too."

Someone else said: "Fascinating stuff. I always assumed that Punch’s features were that of a drunken man (red nose etc) like most clowns."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

What is acromegaly ?

The NHS describes acromegaly as "a rare condition where the body makes too much of a hormone that can make parts of your body grow bigger". It can cause the feet, fingers, head, tongue, and neck to increase in size, as well as abnormal height growth in children and teenagers, also called gigantism.

Actor and wrestler Andre the Giant, who was 7ft 4ins tall, suffered with the condition, as did Richard Kiel, who played the towering villain Jaws in two James Bond films.

Article continues below

Other symptoms can include swollen hands and feet, tiredness or difficulty sleeping, sleep apnoea, sweating, numbness and weakness in the hands, headaches, joint pain, thicker and more oily skin, a deeper voice, irregular periods, and erection problems.

It is usually caused by an adenoma, or a non-cancerous tumour, in the pituitary gland, a pea-sized gland at the back of your brain, causing it to produce too much growth hormone. It is most common between the ages of 30 and 50, but can develop at any age.

Treatments can include surgery to remove the tumour, radiotherapy, and injections or tablets.

News.title: Brits could win back 22 DAYS a year by using their time more effectively on-the-go
News.content:
Brits could win back 22 DAYS a year by using their time more effectively on-the-go

We waste hours every week literally sitting around or getting from one place to another, according to research by VodafoneThree - but there are ways to be more efficient

View 3 Images Tech can help us make more efficient use of our days (Image: Cover Images)

Brits could unlock more than three weeks of unproductive time a year if they could run their lives more effectively from their mobiles on-the-go.

‌



The average person wastes nearly two hours a week on the commute and more than an hour sitting in waiting rooms, according to research by VodafoneThree. Picking up children and other dependents also burns through more than an hour of potentially useful time.

‌



In total, Brits' unproductive time amounts to more than 10 hours a week - far more than Hungary, France, Germany, Spain, Australia, Singapore and South Korea.

‌



View 3 Images VodafoneThree reckons we can carve out more from our time and be happier as a result (Image: Cover Images)

Dog nearly dies after X-ray reveals he swallowed entire rubber duck READ MORE :

If the UK adopted the on-the-go mentality of Hungary - which ranked as the most productive in the study - Brits could claw back 22 days a year.

The knock-on effect is huge, with the country missing out on an annual £115billion boost to the economy because workers are unable to make better use of their time on the move.

‌



Biggest gains could come from simple everyday tasks, such as accessing and collaborating on work documents, taking calls while commuting and joining remote NHS consultations.

The research also found that many Brits still feel tied to fixed locations with a third reluctant to leave their home or office Wi-Fi and almost half tied to their desk for most of their working day.

Lack of flexibility extends beyond the working week with 34% saying their weekend to-do list would be shorter if they could be more productive on the go.

‌



The findings follow a government consultation which focused on supporting investment and innovation in mobile infrastructure to drive growth nationwide.

VodafoneThree is investing £11 billion to improve the UK’s mobile networks, with 5G Standalone coverage set to reach 99% of the population by 2030 and 99.96% by 2034.

The rollout will help Brits work more productively on the go, while boosting access to public services and also cut NHS costs.

‌



View 3 Images Foundations for growth are being laid to help us make better use of our commuting time (Image: Cover Images)

Estimates suggest that improved connectivity could eliminate more than 35million missed remote appointments a year by allowing people to book and reschedule on the go. The potential annual saving is £1.36billion.

Andrea Donà, chief network officer at VodafoneThree, said: “Boosting the UK’s productivity doesn’t have to mean spending more hours behind our desks. But to change the way the nation works, we need mobile networks that keep us connected to colleagues, technology and essential services on the move.

Article continues below

“Our £11 billion network investment is already helping communities across the UK to be more connected, productive and prosperous. But to truly catch up with the rest of Europe and beyond, we have to treat our mobile networks as Critical National Infrastructure.

“The UK Government is rightly taking this issue seriously. With improvements to the planning system and regulations fit for the digital economy, our networks can help to make public services more accessible, close digital divides and lay the foundations for growth.”

News.title: Temporary ban on sale of disposable BBQs over wildfire risk
News.content:
Disposal barbecues have been temporarily banned from sale over fears they pose a "significant risk to the public" as drought and heatwave conditions continue to grip the UK.

They have been the cause of "a number of serious wildfires across the country over the summer months", the government said.

A potential ban was first discussed at an emergency Cobra meeting in response to record temperatures earlier this week. Members of the public have also been urged not to light an open fire of any kind and dispose of cigarettes carefully.

Meanwhile Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the country is like "a tinderbox" as fire crews in the West Midlands continue to battle multiple blazes.

News.title: Chris Mason: Where does this unorthodox by-election victory leave Nigel Farage?
News.content:
It is a question prompting at least some debate within the party.

"When he goes down this angry route he doesn't help himself," the prominent Reform activist Tim Montgomerie told Radio 4's The World At One.

Montgomerie, the founder of the ConservativeHome website, defected to Reform two years ago. He praised Farage's political ability but added: "It's very frustrating how he's behaved today. He needs to get a grip of this problem."

Montgomerie argued Farage and Reform were at their best when they were more positive rather than "inward looking" and focused on "grievances."

The "grievances," as Montgomerie puts it, are real and legitimate, say Farage's friends.

In the short term at least and from a point of weakness I have previously written about, the by-election allowed Farage to get on the front foot and to frame an argument, as he saw it, as the people versus those out to get him.

Rubbish, say his critics, the rules apply to all MPs and the undeclared Â£5m gift from the billionaire businessman Christopher Harborne, in the months before Farage became an MP, should have been registered, they insist.

Talking to GB News in the early hours of this morning, before the result, Farage repeated a concession, of sorts, about this: "If I made one sin, it's that I haven't filled in a piece of paper.

"I've broken no law, I've broken no tax law, I've taken no public money. I don't even own a motor home. Maybe I haven't filled in a piece of paper. I'm confident I'm right - we'll see where we go."

He has long maintained he sought legal advice about whether he needed to declare the money and had been told he didn't.

The wider question is where Nigel Farage and Reform find themselves in the big picture politically and whether their current approach is a wise one.

There is early evidence of something of a Burnham bounce for Labour, which has disrupted Reform's long standing lead in the opinion polls.

And the Conservatives appear more chipper and competitive than a year ago too.

Then there is the rise of Restore Britain, run by the former Reform MP Rupert Lowe.

Let's be clear: none of the political parties are wildly popular at the moment, but Reform's support has shrivelled a bit and their rivals are more upbeat.

The landscape for the new political season at Westminster is taking shape, ahead of MPs returning to the Commons in a few weeks.

Labour with a spring in its step, for now at least. Reform punchy but feeling under the cosh and plenty of the others scrapping for attention too.

It will be a fascinating few months ahead.

News.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
News.content:
Five years on from the Taliban takeover in Afghanistan, women and girls have told the BBC their lives are unrecognisable under the rule of the regime.

The hard-line Islamist group has been eroding the rights of the 22 million women in the country since it re-gained control in 2021- two decades after being removed from power by a US-led military coalition.

The BBC is one of the few media organisations that has been able to maintain access to Afghanistan since the takeover. We spoke to women across the country, from the heart of Kabul to the vast countryside.

They have watched on as the Taliban barred access to school for girls over 12, restricted travel without a male chaperone and brought in a law implying legal approval for child marriage.

When questioned by BBC Afghan over the constraints that women face, the Taliban's foreign minister said: "Women are not totally restricted on all walks of life".

But the restrictions impact almost every part of their lives and make it difficult to tell their stories. Many of the women have not used their real names because they fear reprisals.

"People are so overwhelmed by poverty and daily hardships that many have been forced to put their education, dreams, and hopes for the future aside," Ela from Kabul said.

"Today, survival has become the priority, and many of us no longer have the time or energy to think about the future."

This story contains distressing details.

News.title: Britain's Finlay Tarling dies in Volta a Portugal accident
News.content:
British cyclist Finlay Tarling has died aged 19 after an accident during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

Tarling, the younger brother of Netcompany-Ineos rider Josh, had raced for Great Britain on the road and track.

The Welshman was competing for the NSN Development Team when the incident occurred on the 166.8km route from Melgaco to Fafe.

In a statement, NSN said: "We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

"Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

"Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend."

In a post on X, the race organisers and the Portuguese Cycling Federation expressed their "most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones".

It added that the racing was stopped and the scheduled podium ceremony would not take place as a sign of "respect and mourning".

Portuguese president Antonio Jose Seguro added that Tarling's death had "plunged the peloton, the tournament and the host nation into mourning".

British Cycling's performance director Stephen Park, added: "All of us at British Cycling are heartbroken to learn of the tragic passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal.

"Fin was a talented rider with a fantastic future ahead of him, a loyal teammate and an all-round brilliant young man.

"Our deepest sympathies are with his parents and brother, Josh at this tragic time."

World governing body the UCI added on X: "The UCI is deeply saddened by the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling, who passed away following a serious accident during today's eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

"The UCI extends its deepest condolences to Finlay's family, friends, and team-mates."

The Volta a Portugal got under way in Lisbon on 5 August and is raced over 10 stages, concluding in Porto on 16 August.

Tarling looked to be following in the footsteps of his older brother Josh as a time trial specialist.

He finished in third in the under-23 men's individual time trial at the British Championships in June and competed in the Tour of Britain just under 12 months ago.

News.title: Bezos-backed consortium buys a third of Liverpool FC
News.content:
Liverpool's owners have agreed to sell around a third of the club to a consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

In a statement, Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed it had entered into a "definitive agreement" for the sale of a "strategic minority investment" to 1892 Holdings.

The group is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes billionaire Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Bhatia is set to become Liverpool's vice-chairman, and will join an expanded board pending regulatory approval.

The son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal, he had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.

American businessman Bezos, founder of e-commerce giant Amazon, is the fourth-richest person in the world, with an estimated net worth of $256bn (Â£192bn). This marks his first foray into sports ownership, although he will not join Liverpool's board.

However, Bryan Baum, founder of venture capital firm K5 Sports - through which Bezos is investing - will join the Anfield board, alongside Saverin's wife Elaine.

BBC Sport has been told that the transaction will have no impact on the club's approach to the transfer window, and that there is no new or separate transfer budget associated with the investment.

The agreement includes an option for the consortium to increase its investment in the future. That suggests the group will be in pole position to become majority shareholders if Fenway wants to sell up, but according to one source, no commitments have been made to do so.

The deal is said to value the club between Â£5bn and Â£6bn.

News.title: Stephen Bear jailed over sex offender breaches
News.content:
Reality TV contestant Stephen Bear taunted police by "bragging" he was on a beach in Brazil while he breached his requirements as a sex offender, a court has heard.

He was not on the run during the trip last year, but under the rules of his registration requirements he was ordered to tell authorities about foreign travel.

Bear, 36, admitted five counts of failing to comply with the register notification requirements at Thames Magistrates' Court and was sentenced to 24 weeks in prison.

He is already in prison having been jailed on Thursday after admitting breaching a restraining order that banned him from posting online about his ex-partner Georgia Harrison.

News.title: Prisoners charged over attack on Sara Sharif's father
News.content:
Two prisoners have been charged with the attempted murder of fellow inmate Urfan Sharif who was jailed for killing his daughter Sara Sharif.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, have also been charged with other offences relating to the incident in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

The men will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court for a first hearing on 26 August.

Sharif, 43, and Sara's stepmother Beinash Batool were sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted at the Old Bailey for murdering 10-year-old Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey.

Sharif reportedly suffered cuts to his face during the attack, and received medical treatment at the prison.

Daren Streeter, deputy chief crown prosecutor at CPS London, said: "Our prosecutors have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and pursue criminal proceedings."

Sara was hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in August 2023.

During the trial, Justice Cavanagh told the court "the degree of cruelty involved is almost inconceivable".

Urfan Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for murder, while his wife Beinash Batool, 30, received a minimum of 33 years.

Sara's uncle, Faisal Malik, 29, was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for causing or allowing her death.

The three fled to Islamabad, Pakistan, with Sara's five siblings, the day before her body was found, prompting an international manhunt.

They hid out there for four weeks before returning to the UK, where they were arrested.

News.title: Glastonbury festival organiser dismisses rumours that Madonna will headline in 2027
News.content:
Glastonbury organiser Emily Eavis has said the festival has booked its headliners for next summer - but scotched rumours that Madonna will be among them.

Asked about the 2027 line-up and the speculation that the Queen of Pop would make her Glastonbury debut, Eavis told Katie Razzall on BBC Radio 4's PM programme: "No, it's definitely not Madonna, I'll tell you that.

"But we have got three [other] headliners and we're very excited about it - it's all coming together really well," Eavis added.

And when asked about the possibility of a performance from Taylor Swift, Eavis laughed and said she didn't want to discuss the line-up any more.

News.title: Mother jailed for killing baby by burning her with a hairdryer
News.content:
A mother who killed her baby daughter by burning her with a hairdryer has been jailed for six years.

Courtney Gartshore, 28, used the appliance to subject three-month-old Dahlia-Rose to "significant and sustained heat" on her head and body.

Emergency services were called to the scene at a property in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, in September 2023, but the child had died.

Gartshore was convicted of culpable homicide - the closest equivalent to manslaughter in Scots Law - following a trial at the High Court in Aberdeen in July.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

Sentencing Gartshore at the High Court in Edinburgh, judge Simon Collins KC told her, external she had inflicted "severe and disfiguring" burns on her daughter.

He said: "Given Dahlia-Rose's very young age, and the horrifying way that she died, this is a uniquely disturbing and distressing case.

"But it is tragic as well as terrible. And that is because the evidence suggested that the accused loved Dahlia-Rose, yet will have to live the rest of her life with the knowledge that she was responsible for her death."

News.title: Two dead after light aircraft crash
News.content:
Two people have died following a light aircraft crash in north Wales.

The aircraft was found in a remote location close to Trawsfynydd, near Blaenau Ffestiniog, Gwynedd, with the two people on board pronounced dead at the scene, North Wales Police said.

The force received reports shortly after 12:00 BST that a light aircraft travelling from an airfield in England had not arrived at Caernarfon Airport as scheduled.

Multi-agency air and ground searches were carried out until the aircraft was found.

A team of investigators have since been deployed by the Air Accidents Investigations Branch (AAIB).

Ch Supt Owain Llewellyn said it has been a "challenging search operation".

"Our thoughts are with the families and friends of those involved in this tragic incident," he said.

He added that his force would support the AAIB in its investigation to "ensure the circumstances leading to this incident are fully understood".

He added: "I am grateful to all of the agencies involved for their professionalism and dedication."

News.title: Weekend cancellations after East Sussex train derailment
News.content:
Rail services on a busy line in the South East are being cancelled this weekend after a train carrying 150 people derailed in East Sussex.

Two passengers suffered serious injuries and 18 others were also hurt when three carriages of the train came off the tracks near Lewes on Thursday. Police have since said none of the casualties had life-threatening injuries.

Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) inspectors are at the scene gathering evidence, examining infrastructure and reviewing CCTV, signalling and train data.

The derailment was followed by another incident in Essex on Friday, when a Greater Anglia train came off the tracks near Wickford.
