24 - Bolton Wanderers

I'm backing two of the promoted teams to stay up this year, or at the very least make a good fist of doing so. I'm less optimistic on Bolton, largely because in Amario Cozier-Duberry and Mason Burstow, they will have to make do without two of their most influential attackers from last season. It also feels like a lack of business has been done, particularly in those forward areas.

Ryan Hardie was signed on loan earlier this week and has double figure pedigree at this level but goals may still be hard to come by with loanees Cozier-Duberry and Burstow (their top scorer last term with 12 league goals) not returning. Sam Dalby was next best in the scoring charts with 10 goals but is an unknown quantity at this level. It feels like more firepower is essential before the transfer deadline. David Watson, Ben Davies, Akin Famewo, Luca Stephenson, Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal have all come through the door but none really jump out at you. If any team needs a big final few weeks in the window, it's Bolton.

‌



23 - Charlton Athletic

Charlton got over the line last year after a bit of a slog to give themselves an opportunity to kick on under Nathan Jones. The issue is that they will have to try and do so in a division which feels significantly stronger this time around - and I'm not totally sold on the business they've done being enough to keep their heads above water.

Jones has spoken about Charlton wanting to evolve but it's hard to see where the goals are coming from for them to do so. The Addicks were the third lowest scorers in the division last year; other than Charlie Kelman (7) and Sonny Carey (8) no other Charlton player registered more than three goals in the league. Millenic Alli and Karlan Grant have been brought in to add to Charlton's wide attacking options but the former has a dearth of Championship experience and Grant last hit double figures in the league back in the 2021-22 campaign. Their midfield options don't inspire confidence either; it's one thing questioning whether the strikers can get more goals but the service into them also needs to be better. I'm not seeing that correlation right now.

Charlton will be solid and diligent but I don't think that will be enough. It feels like Jones recognises that with his desire for Charlton to be less limited this year. Have they done the business to do so? It doesn't feel like it.

‌



22 - Lincoln City

View 7 Images Lincoln City went 29 games unbeaten to romp League One last season (Image: PA)

Momentum can be a force of nature in football and it half feels like Lincoln have forgotten how to lose games after going 29 unbeaten to absolutely romp their way to the League One title. But even for one of the most sensible and well-run clubs in the pyramid, take away your manager and star player from that formula and it's a pretty devastating one-two.

The reason I have them in the final relegation spot is that I fancy them to at least give a good fist of upsetting the odds again. However, Jack Moylan was their talisman and his loss is significant, maybe more so than Michael Skubala. On the incoming front, it feels like Tanto Olaofe has the tools to make a nuisance of himself at this level even if he may not be prolific. Mason Melia, the promising young Tottenham striker, is a wildcard in attack after signing on loan. There's not been loads of business done but Lincoln do still have the nucleus of the team that absolutely demolished League One last season.

‌



The step up will be significant and they will undoubtedly become reacquainted with the feeling that comes after losing games. But Lincoln can hold their own and will bloody some noses.

21 - Blackburn Rovers

Blackburn have arguably had the weakest transfer window of any side in the division, adding just Moussa Baradji, Jayden Fevrier and Sam Morsy to a squad that flirted with relegation for most of last season. Already, we're in alarm bell territory.

Tony Mowbray returning to Ewood Park has probably been Blackburn's most significant capture of the summer but the squad he will start the season with is threadbare. Rovers will play on the front foot more under Mowbray and have players who can outscore teams; that will be what sets them apart from others down the bottom. The fact they have attacking players who you would genuinely back to deliver over the course of a season, like Ryoya Morishita, Andri Gudjohnsen and Yuki Ohashi, is encouraging. But they lack depth in other areas and that will prove problematic as the season goes in.

‌



20 - Portsmouth

After two consecutive survival battles, it feels like Portsmouth are trying to kick on this summer by opening up the purse strings, operating at a different level in the transfer market compared to what we have seen previously. Big striker Marko Milovanovic and the all-action midfielder Rocco Shein after intriguing pick ups and the onus will be on the former to hit the ground running to ease some of the goal-scoring burden on Adrian Segecic, who is a right player. A fit and firing Josh Murphy will also go some way to helping on the goal front; plagued by injuries last year, he racked up 22 goal contributions in 45 league games during the 2024-25 campaign.

I think Portsmouth will be okay but I don't see them having the depth to climb the table significantly compared to last year. A lot will hinge on how their new signings adapt. We've seen lots of clubs, Millwall most recently, enjoy success from overseas signings and effective player trading. This year could be Portsmouth's first step in emulating that model, which would serve them well.

19 - Stoke City

‌



It almost feels like Stoke are stuck in some weird sort of Narnia whereby they do business I like each summer but don't tend to go anywhere. Therefore I just can't bring myself to back them for any sort of decent finish.

It's now been nine years since Stoke dropped out of the Premier League and they still haven't recorded a top-half finish in the Championship. Ethan Galbraith quickly established himself as one of the Championship's best playmakers at Swansea after making the step up from Leyton Orient last summer and landing him for big money felt like a real statement of intent at the time. But beyond that I'm not sold on any of their other incoming business. Viktor Johanssen and Million Manhoef are quality and Mark Robins should, theoretically, be the perfect manager to finally get Stoke out of their 14th-18th malaise. Maybe this will be the year. But it'll be a braver man than me who backs it.

18 - Preston North End

A Championship without Preston North End just doesn't feel right. I did initially have fears that could change, but late transfer business has convinced me to nudge them up this list.

‌



Ambition wise, PNE smashed their transfer record to retain the services of star man Alfie Devine after his stellar loan last year earlier this summer. But beyond that, it all felt a bit underwhelming for a while. Delano Burgzorg managed just three Championship goals last season and five the year before, while Jusef Erabi, also joining in attack, is an unknown quantity at this level. Captain Ben Whiteman chucking the towel in a fortnight before the season starts following interest from Wrexham is hardly a resounding vote of confidence for where PNE were at, either.

But they have replaced him swiftly with Leo Leroy from Basel, who looks a good signing. And it was confirmed on Friday that a deal for Stan Mills to join the club in January has been agreed due to Oxford United's current transfer embargo. More could follow before the window shuts. So although the vibes at Deepdale haven't been great throughout the summer, I don't see them in a relegation fight.

17 - Cardiff City

View 7 Images Cardiff City are back in the Championship after winning promotion last season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

‌



Cardiff look by far the best equipped of the promoted sides to cope with life in the Championship and I debated placing the Bluebirds a fair bit higher on the list here. I always think this pool of teams, the ones who won't be troubled by relegation but are perhaps unlikely to mount a realistic play-off push, are the hardest ones to place.

Brian Barry-Murphy's total football should translate well to a higher level and in Yousef Salech they boast a striker whose game will suit the league. Moylan is another player I fancy to replicate his stunning League One form in the Championship, while signing Nathan Trott permanently is huge after his excellent loan last season. Maybe Cardiff can maintain their momentum from last season and push for a higher finish than this. There has also been talk of significant further spending in the transfer market, which could skew these predictions. One thing I am certain of is they won't be looking anxiously over their shoulder.

16 - Watford

Individually, Watford have some proper talent in their squad. But they are another team that you just wouldn't feel comfortable backing to achieve something based on a lots of factors. One big one is the manager: Alessio Dionisi starts the season, but will he end it? Who knows. Probably not even Watford.

‌



Giorgi Chakvetadze and Nestory Irankunda (who is finalising a move to Sporting Lisbon as I finish these predictions) are big losses. Imran Louza would be another with intense speculation over his future. That would be three big losses and probably kill off any outside chance of a play-off push. That being said, who really knows what any season holds for Watford. The only thing I'll stick my neck out and say is that, like Cardiff above, they won't be looking over their shoulder at any point.

15 - Birmingham City

Birmingham will have grand ambitions this season and will be all the better for last year's campaign, where they consolidated themselves in steady if not spectacular fashion. The problem I think they'll find is that there are just too many teams who are better than them currently for them to really kick on this year.

Maybe that sounds harsh. Or lazy. Or both! But I just don't see the significant upturn in points they will require to break into the top eight, although they do have the scope to do something completely bonkers in the final weeks of the transfer window to make me look foolish.

‌



14 - Derby County

Derby came close to the play-offs under John Eustace last year and the nucleus of that squad is still intact. But I think they will be one of the teams who find themselves finishing lower this term simply due to the strength of others.

The unexpected collapse of a takeover by the Saudi Arabian boxing kingpin Turki Alalshikh is likely to have an impact on the club's incoming transfer activity, though they have managed to secure the permanent signings of popular loanees Sammy Szmodics and Bobby Clark. Derby are a strong, powerful team who nobody will fancy playing. And on their day, they are a match for any team in the division. Across the course of a season is another matter, though I wouldn't be too shocked if any of the teams placed between 10 and 14 here end up in slightly different spots.

13 - Bristol City

‌



It felt like Bristol City needed a big summer after falling away bigtime last year and, on paper, they've delivered. They've spent the best part of £9million on League One's two top strikers in Dom Ballard and Lorent Tolaj. Plus they've brought in the highly-rated Sam Tickle as their new No 1 keeper, the industrious Sam Greenwood to further strengthen in the attacking areas and Championship stalwart Jed Wallace. On paper, not bad, right?

Does all that equate to a play-off finish under the guidance of new head coach, Michael Skubala? Maybe. I still reckon Bristol City fall just short, mainly due to the strength of the division. There are just too many good teams ahead of them and, let's not forget, they are effectively ripping things up and starting again with Skubala at the helm. A top eight finish at the first time of asking is probably a stretch, but a good season here should set them up nicely for next year.

12 - West Brom

View 7 Images James Morrison will lead West Brom permanently after keeping them up last season (Image: Adam Fradgley/West Bromwich Albion FC)

‌



James Morrison is one of the big unknown quantities ahead of the new season. His arrival as caretaker boss was the catalyst for West Brom retaining their Championship status after a truly chastening campaign He rightly landed the job on a full-time basis off the back of that, but can he now oversee a promotion challenge?

The Baggies went back to basics under Morrison in a bid to accumulate the points necessary to stay afloat and it remains to be seen if they will stick with the same approach given the former midfielder has now effectively been given a blank canvas to work with. Squad-wise, West Brom have good players and better depth than some others. Does that translate into a top eight finish? I'm unsure, so I'll hedge my bets.

11 - Swansea City

Swansea start the season with perhaps the best striker in the division in Zan Vipotnik. But will they end the window with last season's Championship top scorer still in tow with Hull City circling? That remains to be seen and plays a factor here.

‌



Keeping Vipotnik would be a major transfer win and they've done smart business too: Elijah Just looked a right player at the World Cup and will bolster their attack and if they can keep Ross Stewart fit after snapping the striker up from Sunderland, then it could be the signing of the summer. Unfortunately, it's at the other end Swansea look less convincing. The news on the eve of the new season that Cameron Burgess has suffered an ACL injury isn't particularly helpful for Vitor Matos.

10 - Wrexham

Wrexham came agonisingly close to landing a play-off spot last season and will be in the mix to go one better this season. But again, the quality of the other teams pushing for those top eight positions could just nudge Phil Parkinson's team aside.

After hitting their stride in the second half of last term, Wrexham have opted for continuity and strengthened smartly rather than opting for full-scale surgery. Danny Imray is an excellent pick-up at right-back and will enhance their attacking threat from that area. Anthony Patterson will come in as first-choice keeper and is an upgrade on last season. Josh Windass will lead from the front again after bagging an impressive 17 goals last season with only Vipotnik, Ollie McBurnie and Haji Wright netting more. Kieffer Moore and Sam Smith will provide support but I reckon a marquee addition in attack is needed for them to gatecrash the top eight this time.

‌



9 - QPR

View 7 Images QPR could be dark horses for a top eight finish (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

In terms of transfer window wins, QPR are right up there. Looking at their business, there is a lot to like: Pierce Charles on loan feels shrewd, albeit the youngster dropped a clanger in the cup game with Millwall. Picking up Dennis Cirkin on a free transfer is just tremendous business and Tariq Lamptey could still be a game-changer if he can rediscover his fitness and hit top form again. Glenn Kamara also adds some steel in midfield.

The bonus QPR have despite their form absolutely falling off a cliff at the end of last season (and largely why I'm choosing to ignore that) is that they already have an adequate attacking arsenal to compliment their new signings. Richard Kone and Rumarn Burrell should both be in the goals after acclimatising to Championship level last term and are backed up by the likes of Karomoko Dembele, Kwame Poku and Koki Saito. And Illias Chair. What does that all up to? My prediction is QPR will be a good watch and dark horses for a top eight finish.

‌



8 - Sheffield United

Sheffield United were an absolute calamity last season and probably ruined many an ante-post bet. They were steady if unspectacular following Chris Wilder's return and feel safer to back this time around, albeit with the caveat that troubling the top two feels beyond them.

The incoming business so far doesn't feel like much to crow about, while the sale of Andre Brooks to Norwich was a painful one. But the team that finished the season is far superior than their final league standing of 13th. This time around, Wilder and Co won't be playing catch up after the sort of nightmare start even a depressed supercomputer would struggle to realistically muster up. They've lost Gustavo Hamer, but the squad still boasts plenty of firepower and players who have experience of doing the business at this level. Defensively they have some of the division's top performers in their respective positions in keeper Michael Cooper, Japhet Tanganga and Femi Seriki. That's a nice mix and I reckon they return to the pack challenging for promotion.

7 - Burnley

‌



Of all the relegated sides, Burnley feel like the hardest to predict. They are not the only club to head into the season with a manager who is untested on these shores but it feels like Nicky Hayen has a bigger job on his hands than Cesar Peixoto. If they retain the services of Zian Flemming, then Burnley could finish higher. They absolutely haemorrhaged goals last season - almost two a game - but I like the loan signing of Max Alleyne from Manchester City.

Cards on the table time: I really don't know what to expect from Burnley and they were by far the hardest to place on this list. My gut and head says they will not be the force they usually are in this division after dropping down. I had a couple of absolute shockers last year and Burnley could very well be the shout I try to avoid looking at for the next 12 months.

6 - Millwall

Millwall enjoyed their best campaign in a generation last time out as they defied all the odds to finish third, missing out on automatic promotion on the final day. Emulating that feat will take some doing, even though the nucleus of the squad that won more games than any other team in the division bar champions Coventry City largely remains.

‌



Talisman Femi Azeez is likely to depart and losing his ability to conjure up something from nothing in the final third will hurt a team who were the lowest scorers in the top eight. On paper, Millwall's incoming business looks positive and you can tell from their recent track record in the transfer market that they generally know what they're doing on that front. They also boast one of the division's top managers in Alex Neil, who underlined his credentials with last year's showing. The squad does feel imbalanced, though, with just two out and out senior wingers in Azeez and Kyrell Lisbie. And with Azeez likely to depart and Tristan Crama recently undergoing ankle surgery, Millwall will be without the dynamic right hand pairing that was so influential last term.

The Lions may not finish as high as last year, but another play-off finish feels within reach and would represent another strong season.

5 - Southampton

View 7 Images Tonda Eckert remains in charge of Southampton but he could face a ban over 'Spygate' (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

‌



Southampton were absolutely motoring at the end of last season and probably have the squad to finish better than the fifth place I've got them down for. But the uncertainty over Tonda Eckert plays a big role in that; if the German is handed a ban for the Spygate scandal that marred last year's play-offs, then that could skew Southampton's season massively. The shadow of that possibility even hanging over them might even do the trick.

Regardless of who is at the helm, Southampton won't be on minus points for long and will be among the teams slugging it out for promotion. It's hard to pinpoint a weakness in the squad: Daniel Peretz is back permanently and we already know his quality, while Cyle Larin, Lewis Dobbin and Divin Mubama give the Saints even more firepower. The squad is just a joke all around, really. Leo Scienza and Tom Fellows on either flank...forget the spying, are we sure that's allowed? Really, it's a poor season for Southampton if they are in the play-off eliminators. If the Eckert situation had been resolved and there was clarity on that front, I've have them well clear of them.

4 - Norwich City

Under Philippe Clement, Norwich feel like proper promotion contenders. The former Rangers boss inherited a team in turmoil with Norwich second from bottom after failing to win a staggering seven straight home games in the Championship. He would oversee 17 wins from 31 games, which is promotion form.

‌



I feel like a broken record banging on about strikers and firepower, but goals win prizes and Norwich have some seriously heavy artillery up top. Jovon Mokoma is the business and should be a decent shout for top scorer, while Mo Toure has adapted to the Championship seamlessly. Norwich are less convincing at the other end and will ship goals. But for every goal they concede they could go and score three. I can see them troubling the top, top dogs but having to settle for a play-off spot, eventually. Again, think they will be a really good watch for any neutrals who find themselves flicking through Sky Sports + via the red button on midweeks.

3 - West Ham

I know, I know: West Ham was the banker. This was the no-brainer, the one that couldn't fail etc etc. If we're speaking about absolute jokes of a squad then West Ham are bang up there in terms of invidual players (Jarrod Bowen in the Champ? Come on). And yet I think that's also part of the reason why a top two finish could elude them. They have the tools to succeed but does it all work together?

Nuno Espirito Santo has been there, done that, got that t-shirt when it comes to promotion from the Championship, so he's not walking into the unknown. But the landscape has changed drastically since then. West Ham in the Championship now feels far more significant than it did when they were last in here more than a decade ago and the dynamics have shifted; if they attempt to continue with the same pragmatic style Nuno has typically deployed throughout his career, then I don't see them doing enough to crack the top two. And that's before we even touch on the weight of expectation that will be on them and their manager. With respect, Wolves in the Championship at the time was a big job. But this feels like another level for him and a group of players who went down last year.

‌



I don't mean to go into full-on cliche mode, but how will this star-studded squad cope with being the scalp of the division? Can they, in fact, do it on a cold Tuesday night away at Stoke? Maybe I'm wrong and West Ham will absolutely romp it. But coming off the back of a bruising relegation and with off-field drama still prevalent in the background, I'm not sure it'll be as straightforward as some are expecting.

2 - Middlesbrough

You've got to give it to Boro - they have had the sort of transfer window that wouldn't look out of place in Football Manager (the good ones, not 2026). They've scooped major windfalls from sell-on clauses, banked a tidy sum from the sale of their talisman Hayden Hackney (bittersweet but necessary as his deal was up next year) and they've used it to level up in the two positions that cost them automatic promotion last year in goalkeeper and striker.

Radek Vitek is a huge upgrade on Sol Brynn and will be one of the division's top keepers, while Will Lankshear should absolutely feast if he is served up the same number of quality chances that Boro's forward's spurned last season. Just the impact from those two alone will serve Boro incredibly well. We know the squad is strong, even though the loss of Hackney is a huge blow.

‌



Backing Boro to finish second ahead of some of the other quality teams in this league might feel bold, but the team and manager Kim Hellberg are impressive. And while others, like the teams coming down, may have to find their feet back at the level, Middlesbrough should get motoring far quicker.

1 - Wolves

View 7 Images Wolves are likely to be in the frame for an instant return to the Premier League (Image: David Rogers)

Wolves needed a huge revamp after one of the worst Premier League seasons in history…that hasn’t happened. Wolves needed to shift the deadwood and high earners out of the club…that hasn’t happened either. So why - I hear you ask - are we tipping Cesar Peixoto’s side to finish at the top of the Championship pile?

‌



Simply put, Wolves have an embarrassment of riches for the second tier. In midfield, they have a Brazilian international in Andre, the exciting Fer Lopez and potentially Jordan James. Signing Kieran Trippier was an impressive coup, bringing Raul Jimenez back to Molineux was potentially even more eye-catching. Adam Armstrong, who was on course to be the league’s top scorer before moving to Molineux in the 2025/26 campaign, may have to settle for a place on the bench this time around.

Pre-season has shown Wolves will play on the front foot and press high, a method which has worked for previous title winners. They will need to start well to ease the toxicity and could still do with a new keeper and centre back, but Wolves will fancy their chances of lifting the trophy next May.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola to Liverpool transfer twist as decision made over £145m PSG demand
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola to Liverpool transfer twist as decision made over £145m PSG demand

Bradley Barcola has been Liverpool's priority transfer target for the summer window but a bold decision looks to have been made on the Paris Saint-Germain star

View 2 Images Liverpool have made a big decision in their transfer pursuit of Bradley Barcola (Image: (Photo by Maciej Rogowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images))

Liverpool have chosen to pause transfer negotiations for Bradley Barcola with Paris Saint-Germain still demanding £145million. The Reds have been strongly linked to Barcola over the last few weeks as they look to strengthen in attack after Yan Diomande opted to join Real Madrid over both them and PSG.

‌



Luis Enrique's side are currently in the process of finalising two incomings with Mika Godts joining from Ajax and Ferran Torres on his way to the European champions from Barcelona.

‌



Maghnes Akliouche has already joined from AS Monaco, which suggests Barcola, who did not play in their UEFA Super Cup final win over Aston Villa, could be free to leave.

‌



L'Equipe have claimed that Liverpool are yet to find a breakthrough in talks and will thus wait until the final days of the window before restarting their attempts to sign him.

Steven Gerrard lands new job as career takes a twist before Premier League season READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

PSG are currently holding firm on their sizeable financial demands despite his unwillingness to sign a new contract. The Frenchman is reportedly open to an Anfield switch but Liverpool are not currently bending to their demands, seemingly in the hope their asking price decreases.

‌



With roughly £150m to be spent on attackers, it is fair to assume that the Parisians may need to sell and will accept a fee lower below their current demands, but it is certainly a big risk to take.

Having parted ways with Mohamed Salah, Liverpool need to sign a new elite-level forward particularly with Tottenham showing a keen interest in Cody Gakpo.

Diomande was an option before Real paid £120million to sign from RB Leipzig. Barcola and his club teammate Ibrahim Mbaye have subsequently emerged as options. The latter was also an unused substitute against Unai Emery's side.

‌



View 2 Images Ibrahim Mbaye has also been linked with Liverpool

Liverpool have not been too active in the window thus far with Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo the only signings made this summer.

The latter is the second new defender into Anfield, however, with an agreement reached to sign Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes back in February.

Article continues below

Departures and rumours surrounding Liverpool players have been more prominent with Curtis Jones still a target of Inter Milan and Gakpo potentially set to join Spurs.

Sports.title: Galatasaray reject £111m Victor Osimhen transfer offer as Arsenal task made clear
Sports.content:
Galatasaray reject £111m Victor Osimhen transfer offer as Arsenal task made clear

Arsenal are open to the signing of Victor Osimhen as they hold transfer talks with Galatasaray - but the Turkish club have reportedly turned down an offer of £111m for the Nigerian already this summer

View 2 Images Victor Osimhen is on Arsenal's radar, but will command a huge fee (Image: Getty Images)

Galatasaray have already turned down a bid of £111million from Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for Victor Osimhen - underlining the challenge facing Arsenal.

‌



The Gunners have expressed an interest in the Nigerian striker as they negotiate with the Turkish side, who themselves are keen on some of Arsenal's stars. Galatasaray are determined to keep hold of their star striker and do not want to sell him.

‌



And their decision to knock back over £100m this summer suggests Arsenal will have to go well beyond that to sign Osimhen, which in itself would be a club-record spend.

‌



The ex-Napoli striker has been linked with a Premier League switch previously in his career, once being firmly on Chelsea's radar, but when his time in Italy was up he moved to Galatasaray, where he's helped them become champions. The 27-year-old scored 22 goals in all competitions last season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arsenal remain in talks with the Turkish side as they look to offload Gabriel Martinelli and, possibly, Ethan Nwaneri, reports The Sun. Galatasaray have indicated they would pay around £38m for Martinelli, who was once a favourite at the Gunners but has since fallen down the pecking order. It would still represent a major profit for Arsenal, who signed the Brazilian in 2019.

‌



Nwaneri is another player to lose out as a result of Arsenal's aggressive transfer business in recent years. The teenager had to head to Marseille last term and, now back in north London, is thought to prefer a move to Germany if he does leaves Arsenal. Both Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig are keen.

Mikel Arteta is in the market for a marquee attacker this summer and has missed out on the likes of Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior. Both would've represented blockbuster transfers with Rogers ultimately moving to Chelsea for a British-record fee.

View 2 Images Arsenal are in talks with Galatasaray over a move for Gabriel Martinelli (Image: Getty Images)

‌



It is reported that Arsenal refused to match Chelsea on price with their fee going beyond their valuation of Rogers. Osimhen, approaching his prime, is a different type of attacking player and strikers would guarantee goals are among the most expensive assets on the market.

Arsenal spent £64m to land Viktor Gyokeres last summer but the Swede wasn't entirely convincing in his debut year at the Emirates. He was overlooked for the Champions League final and Arteta is ultimately keen on adding more firepower.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo married in front of just FOUR witnesses and signed pre-nup
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo married in front of just FOUR witnesses and signed pre-nup

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez tied the knot in a vert intimate ceremony with just four witnesses present whilst the pair kept their assets separate as they penned a pre-nup

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodrigeuz tied the knot a year after their engagement

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez got married at their new £30million mansion near Lisbon in front of just four witnesses and their children.

‌



Cristiano’s doting mum Dolores Aveiro and his three siblings Hugo, Elma and Katia, were not present at the intimate civil ceremony which took place at 1.30pm on Tuesday.

‌



Georgina’s sister Ivana, Cristiano’s long-time friend Miguel Paixao and a Spanish couple named as Jose Rodriguez Sangil and his wife Monica Goncalez Martinez were the only witnesses.

‌



Registrar Maria Manuel Ferreira de Campos Folhadela de Oliveira travelled from the northern Portuguese city of Porto to Cascais to officiate the ceremony.

And the star couple, who married exactly one year to the day after they announced their engagement on social media, have decided to keep their pre-nuptial assets separate despite tying the knot after a decade-long romance.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



They signed a pre-nup agreement to define their property regime on August 10 a day before the ceremony at a public notary’s office in Lisbon. Ronaldo’s representatives had confirmed earlier this week the footballer and his long-time partner married on August 11 in an “intimate” ceremony in Cascais after the couple posted photos of them wearing their wedding rings on their Instagrams.

It followed speculation which turned out to be false that they were due to marry at Funchal Cathedral in Cristiano's native island of Madeira on Saturday. No details had emerged about where in Cascais they had wed or who exactly was at the ceremony apart from their children.

Overnight, respected Portuguese newspaper Jornal de Noticias published a copy of the marriage certificate showing it took place at Cristiano’s massive built-from-scratch mansion in the upmarket residential area of Quinta da Marina.

‌



View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo's new wife shared a photograph of the couple's wedding rings (Image: Instagram / Georginagio)

And it also evidenced the fact so few people were invited there appeared to be no place for Cristiano’s mum, who gave the union her blessing shortly afterwards by posting a heart emoticon on her son's Instagram in response to his wedding announcement, or the rest of his family apart from his kids. Jose Rodriguez Sangil was described as a Spanish jeweller by Portuguese press.

The marriage document listed Cristiano’s full name and age of 41 as well as his birthplace and the names of his parents including his late father Jose Dinis. The same details were listed for 32-year-old Georgina, born in the Argentinian capital Buenos Aires and referenced by her full name of Georgina Luisa Rodriguez Hernandez.

‌



They will both keep their pre-marriage names, unlike in the UK where newly-married women normally take their husband’s surnames. The marriage certificate was recorded as number 1,493 of this year but appears to have been listed at Porto’s Registry Office instead of Cascais which is the municipality where the wedding took place.

Cristiano and George are now back in Saudi Arabia where the Portuguese international plays his club football for Al Nassr, ahead of the start of the new season.

Sports.title: Man Utd star says being fourth choice is 'not deflating' and explains reasons for staying
Sports.content:
Man Utd star says being fourth choice is 'not deflating' and explains reasons for staying

Manchester United's Dermot Mee helped them see off Leeds during the week and the young goalkeeper insists he's more than happy to be the club's fourth choice shotstopper

View 2 Images Dermot Mee helped Man Utd claim victory over Leeds in their most recent pre-season game

Manchester United goalkeeper Dermott Mee insists he happily signed a new deal knowing he would be the club's fourth choice - which he claims is "not deflating".

‌



The Northern Irishman was given a rare outing as he played in United's pre-season victory over Leeds at Croke Park in Dublin. He was afforded his moment in the spotlight as the game, which ended 1-1 after 90 minutes, went to penalties.

‌



Mee was able to produce the crucial saves which handed United victory in their penultimate pre-season victory. The 23-year-old recently extended his deal at Old Trafford, but did so knowing he would be fourth in the pecking order.

‌



Senne Lammens has established himself as the team's No.1 and underneath him Michael Carrick has Karl Darlow, who arrived on a free this summer, and veteran Tom Heaton.

Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview READ MORE :

Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear READ MORE :

It means Mee will need a fair chunk of luck to go his way if he's to enjoy any notable minutes this term, but he was not put off by his standing within the squad and was determined to remain with his boyhood club. He even went as far to suggest that his role was made harder than many would think.

"You have to think about every contract you sign, whether it's an insurance contract or a football contract," he said. "You just have to weigh up the pros and cons.

‌



"For me, being at Manchester United since 11, it was really hard to turn down. I love the club, I love being here, and I want to help the team to do really well this season. It's not deflating. From the outside it seems a lot harder than it is.

View 2 Images Senne Lammens has established himself as the clear first choice at Old Trafford

"I train every day with some of the best players in the world, so if anything, that could be harder than stepping into the games and being on the bench and being ready."

Article continues below

United have just allowed Radek Vitek to join Middlesbrough whilst Andre Onana has headed back out on loan to Trabzonspor for the second straight year. The Cameroonian's move to Manchester has failed to work out, leaving the club searching for a safe pair of hands for two years now. Altay Bayindir has also moved on.

Sports.title: Liverpool takeover Q&A: What do we know about Bezos' consortium?
Sports.content:
Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group have sold a stake in Liverpool Football Club to a consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

The world's third richest person is part of the group fronted by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia. Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also part of the syndicate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Vinny O'Connor explains why FSG have sold a minority stake in Liverpool to the Bezos-backed consortium

According to Sky News, the consortium has agreed to buy a roughly one-third stake in the club in a deal that values Liverpool at more than 7bn (£5.2bn). Closing of the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

We take a look at some of the key questions surrounding what the deal could look like...

Who are Bezos and Bhatia?

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur, who has an investment banking background.

Image: Amit Bhatia is the former co-owner of Queen's Park Rangers

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital which invests in range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

He leads and manages 1892 Holdings, the consortium that has agreed the minority investment in Liverpool with majority owners Fenway Sports Group.

What are they worth?

Forbes estimates that Bezos' personal fortune is in the region of $281bn (£209bn), making him the third-richest person in the world behind Elon Musk and Google co-founder Larry Page.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News' Mark Kleinman discusses Amazon founder Bezos' involvement in the consortium

It's unclear how much Bhatia himself is worth. But his father-in-law, billionaire steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, is worth an estimated £23.2bn according to Forbes. That makes him the 72nd richest person in the world.

What are their sporting interests?

Bezos is a big American Football fan and has previously been reported to have explored bids for the Washington Commanders and the Seattle Seahawks.

He is not known to hold a significant stake in any other sports team or enterprise currently.

Image: Bezos is known to be a big American Football fan

Bhatia was just 28 when he joined the board of directors and became vice-chairman of QPR in 2007 after the Mittal family bought a 20 per cent stake in QPR, joining Bernie Ecclestone and Flavio Briatore as investors in the London club.

He spent five years as QPR chairman between 2018 and 2023 and stayed on as a director and co-owner until earlier this week when he transferred his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a closer look at Amit Bhatia

Through AyBe capital, Bhatia is an investor in TGL - Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods' golf league which fuses golf and technology and features six teams with some of the best players in the world in a season-long competition.

His firm also invests in Switch Hitter, which is a media brand founded by Kevin Pietersen, delivering exclusive interviews and content with the world's top cricketers.

Image: Rajasthan Royals were one of the most sought-after IPL cricket franchises

Earlier this year, Bhatia's father-in-law acquired a 75 per cent stake in the Rajasthan Royals Indian Premier League cricket franchise.

Why have FSG decided to sell?

FSG were under no pressure to sell but did indicate in 2022 that they were open to new investment in Liverpool, with the sale of a small stake to Dynasty Equity completed the following year.

Liverpool have enjoyed huge success under FSG, lifting every major trophy available to win.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Football finance expert Kieran Maguire explains what a 'strategic minority stake' is

FSG may think it is mission accomplished somewhat as far they are concerned, and therefore were amenable to fresh investment. They also stand to make a huge profit on their initial investment, with the deal for a 30 per cent stake worth more than five times what they paid for the entire club back in 2010.

How much have the consortium bought?

According to Sky News, the consortium is acquiring a roughly one-third stake in the club.

What is the club valued at?

Liverpool are the fourth most valuable club in the world. The consortium's investment in Liverpool values the club somewhere in the region of £5.2bn ($7bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Who owns Liverpool?

FSG have complete operational control of Liverpool, but private equity firms RedBird Capital and Arctos Sports Partners hold minority stakes in the club. Dynasty Equity are also passive investors in Liverpool after injecting £164m into the club in 2023 in a deal valuing Liverpool at more than $4.5bn.

Image: The Anfield home of Liverpool Football Club

How much did FSG pay for Liverpool?

FSG were known as New England Sports Ventures when they paid £300m for Liverpool in October 2010 after a tumultuous period under former owners Tom Hicks and George Gillette.

When will the deal go through?

The deal - which was first reported on at the end of last month - has accelerated at a rapid pace. Now that everything has been agreed, the closing of the transaction will happen after regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions are met.

Who else is involved?

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin and his wife Elaine are also part of the syndicate of investors. Saverin, 44, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

Sports.title: Glave: From 2022 in a back brace to European champion - 'Delayed but not denied'
Sports.content:
Britain's Romell Glave: From two serious back injuries and 2022 in a back brace to European 100m champion - 'Delayed but not denied'

Romell Glave chats exclusively to Sky Sports following his 100m European Athletics success

"2026 was my year of redemption," Romell Glave exclusively tells Sky Sports two days on from when he stood on the podium draped with a 100m gold medal at the European Championships.

The 26-year-old's story and journey to the point of becoming European champion in athletics' marquee event is a remarkable one. "Delayed but not denied," Glave says, with a twinkle in his eye.

Born in Manchester, Jamaica, Glave moved to the UK at the age of 15, joined Croydon Harriers, and by the age of 17 was the fastest 100m sprinter on the planet for his age group, clocking a time of 10.21.

Injuries hit regularly and harshly over the intervening years. So much so that he spent the majority of 2022 in a back brace having fractured vertebrae - issues first occurring when he was forced to train on grass due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

His back injury meant he was only able to make his European Championship debut for Britain in 2024, aged 24.

At that competition, Glave qualified for the 100m final and claimed the bronze medal in a tight race, but though a quest for more followed, he then fractured and inflamed his back for a second time, forcing him to miss out on the Olympic Games in Paris.

In 2026, he returned with a vengeance to succeed. He won gold in the 60m at a World Indoor Athletics meet in Stockholm - defeating Olympic silver medallist Kishane Thompson. He broke the 10-second barrier legally for the first time when he ran 9.98 to win the British title in June, and lowered his personal best again to 9.97 in London the following month.

All his work then culminated in European Championship 100m gold in Birmingham on Tuesday.

"It's been a journey and a half and also a total rollercoaster," Glave tells Sky Sports. "And I know success was a long time coming.

"I just needed to stay healthy because I knew that with the support I've had for the last three years since I had my back fracture, from medical staff like Nick Allen and Peter Horobin who have been there for me, I had a great chance.

Glave was the world's fastest 17-year-old but injuries held him back up to now

"To be able to stand here as a European champion means a lot. It's testament to the hard work they put in to get me to the line and also to keep showing up for me because without them, I don't know if this would be possible.

"It's been a euphoric moment for me, an unreal feeling. Just a feeling of relief the job is accomplished. This is why we do this sport, it means so much to me."

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

'2026 was my year of redemption - nothing was stopping me from succeeding'

Hit by one injury knockback after another, many athletes may even have called it quits.

Instead, Glave tackled 2026 with an intensive determination to succeed. So much so that even when doubts, nerves or physical issues crept in he was able to channel them out.

It was notable watching the start line to the 100m final just how relaxed Glave appeared, a state very difficult to achieve ahead of an event that means so much and that he would have worked so hard towards. But this was an athlete totally in flow.

"I would say I came into this season just to show a bit of redemption after the loss of years, loss of seasons to injury," Glave says.

"But to also start this season with a very resilient mindset of: 'I want to go for everything.' I was a 2024 bronze medallist at the European Championships and missed the gold medal by a small margin. So why not dream bigger and upgrade my medal to gold?

"That was the aim and objective for the season, from the start of the season. To be European champion and to be able to walk away from from that 100m being crowned king of Europe. It's an amazing feeling.

"It brings me calmness. I've been dreaming of this moment and to be able to live it, it's very surreal.

Glave and British team-mate Jeremiah Azu finished first and second in the 100m final

"Over the last few days, I have had discomfort in my abdominal muscles, but I was not going to let that stop me from obtaining my objective.

"I was able to go out there, regardless of how I was feeling, the discomfort I was enduring, and just focus on the job that was presented in front of me. I got the job done.

"I was ready for this moment, this occasion. I was ready mentally, most importantly, regardless of how I was feeling emotionally or physically, I wasn't going to let that take away the moment from me because I prepared all season long for it.

"This season was all about redemption, that's the theme, and speaking to my sports psychologist, we've been working on all of those formulas to make sure I'm preparing the best way possible to get through."

Glave has tackled 2026 in sensational fashion after a devastating turn in 2024 saw him miss the Olympics

'2024 back injury left a void in my heart'

Thinking back, Glave lays bare the inner turmoil he experienced having battled through one serious back injury, won a European Championship bronze, but then suffered with his back again to miss an Olympics Games and virtually have to start his career all over again.

"It was very disappointing. After the 2024 European Championships, I could feel I was on that momentum, because the trials were two weeks afterwards.

"My first session back after I was crowned European bronze medallist, I picked up the injury and it was a very sad moment for me. My mind went to missing the Olympics, because everyone trains towards going to that.

"And to get a European bronze and have that momentum going into the Olympics, that's what everyone wants. To cut the journey short at that moment, it left a a void in my heart. I'm never going to get that moment back, that's gone."

Glave had to endure a career filled with serious injuries and setbacks

One man Glave has repeatedly singled out in the aftermath of his success has been coach Michael Afilaka, someone he describes as more than just his sprint coach: "a mentor, life coach, a man of wisdom and integrity."

Indeed, referencing his working relationship with Afilaka from serious injury to European champion proves very emotional for Glave.

"He's been doing this for over 20 years and is a private person, but God presented him to me on this journey. Having him beside me has been a life-changing decision.

"During those darkest times of my life, he's the only that is there. His belief, his dedication to continue to show up for me, I haven't really seen that before. I haven't really seen it in my life, in the way he has shown up.

"It's very emotional just talking about it every time, because he didn't have to do it, but because of his persona, he wants the best for me."

Glave spoke emotionally about the time and support coach Michael Afilaka has afforded him

'The next goal is world domination'

In terms of what's next, Glave is clear. He wants to challenge on a world level at the top of the sport.

"World domination is now the main goal, but just to have this stepping stone as European champion, I'm focusing on one step at a time.

"This season is like a stepping stone of what is to come for Romell Glave. I'm in a historic British team and now have the ultimate chance as well.

"So to be there and show up in a field of world-class athletes, that's the main objective now. To perform against those athletes, the world's best."

Sports.title: Gay bags pair in Test warm-up as Pakistan captain Babar suffers injury scare
Sports.content:
England opener Emilio Gay bagged a pair and Pakistan captain Babar Azam suffered an injury scare on an eventful second day of the Test match-warm up in Beckenham.

Gay, having been dismissed by Mohmmad Abbas on day one while batting for a County Select XI against Pakistan, snicked Mohmmad Ali behind on Friday to fall for a seven-ball duck.

The Durham batter had suffered a shoulder injury playing for his county in the One Day Cup earlier this month but his appearance in this game has probably allayed any fears over his fitness for the first Test at Headingley from next Wednesday, live on Sky Sports.

Babar, meanwhile, was struck on the right hand by a delivery from young Hampshire seamer Manny Lumsden and retired hurt on five from 17 balls.

A statement from Pakistan later said that the skipper would sit out the remainder of the game as a precautionary measure but that he will participate in the team's practice session in Leeds on Monday.

Image: Pakistan captain Babar Azam will play no further part in the Test warm-up after being struck on the hand

Babar - whose side also play England at Lord's (from August 27) and Edgbaston (from September 9) - struck one four in Beckenham batting in the No 4 spot.

Pakistan plummeted from 164-2 to 238 all out, in reply to their hosts' initial 305 all out, as they surrendered a 67-run deficit on first innings.

England spinner Shoaib Bashir, hoping to be included in his country's XI at Headingley, bagged figures of 4-76 from 20.2 overs, dismissing opener Imam-ul-Haq (37), middle-order man Salman Ali Agha (14) and then Aamir Jamal (8) and Ghazi Ghori (27).

Abdullah Shafique (61) top-scored for Pakistan, while Lumsden and Northamptonshire's Saif Zaib picked up two wickets apiece for the County Select XI.

The home team extended their advantage to 195 runs by stumps after closing on 128-3 with James Rew (40), Caleb Falconer (52no) - the Middlesex youngster notching his second half-century of the game - and Zaib (24no) chipping in once Gay and opening partner Tom Haines (12) departed cheaply.

Sports.title: Stokes' Durham progress with Flintoff unable to repeat hundred heroics
Sports.content:
A Durham side featuring Ben Stokes thrashed Lancashire by 169 runs to reach the One Day Cup semi-finals with Rocky Flintoff unable to repeat his hundred heroics from earlier in the week.

​​​​​Flintoff, the 18-year-old son of England great Andrew Flintoff, cracked a 65-ball century for Lancashire against Somerset in the final round of group games on Tuesday as he registered his first senior professional ton.

However, the teenager was out for 22 from 39 balls versus Durham at Emirates Old Trafford - one of four wickets taken by Afghan leg-spinner Shafiqullah Ghafari - as Lancashire were bundled out for 187 chasing 350 for victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Rocky Flintoff, son of former England captain Andrew, hit his maiden senior professional century for Lancashire against Somerset with 123 off 76 balls

Quiet day for Stokes but Durham hammer Lancashire

Former England captain Stokes took one wicket, that of opening batter Harry Singh for 11, as he returned figures of 1-32 from four overs after earlier hitting one six in a knock of 11 from nine balls in Durham's 349-6 in Manchester.

Durham - who will now face Middlesex in a semi-final at Radlett on Sunday - saw David Bedingham strike 104 from 89 balls and Ollie Robinson make 76 from 57 deliveries.

The pair shared a fourth-wicket stand of 149 before Robinson's dismissal brought Stokes to the crease.

In reply, only 17-year-old Joe Moores (51 off 42), who stitched a 59-run stand with Flintoff, made a score of note.

Sports.title: SunRisers into Hundred women's final with tense win over Brave
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds booked a meeting with Trent Rockets in The Hundred women's final after a tense five-wicket win over Southern Brave in the eliminator at The Kia Oval.

Set a modest 115 to win, SunRisers had looked in trouble at 54-3 after 47 balls - their dynamic Australian duo of Phoebe Litchfield (4) and Annabel Sutherland (17 off 12) both dismissed - and again at 95-5 after 78 when the impressive Issy Wong (3-21) took two wickets in two balls.

Wong, who had earlier claimed the key wicket of tournament leading run-scorer Litchfield, also bowled Lauren Winfield-Hill (37 off 37) and saw off SunRisers skipper Dani Gibson, lbw first ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Issy Wong took three wickets during The Hundred eliminator between SunRisers Leeds and Southern Brave

But India's Deepti Sharma kept a calm head, her unbeaten 28 off 22 ultimately seeing SunRisers over the line with 11 balls to spare and into Sunday's final at Lord's.

Score Summary - SunRisers Leeds vs Southern Brave Southern Brave 114-7 from 100 balls: Lizelle Lee (32 off 25 balls); Hannah Baker (2-13), Annabel Sutherland (2-31) SunRisers Leeds 116-5 from 89 balls: Lauren Winfield-Hill (37 off 37 balls), Deepti Sharma (28no off 22); Issy Wong (3-21)

The result was in keeping with the form guide, with the tournament's early pace-setters Brave losing a fourth straight match after starting with five wins from five.

SunRisers are defending champions - having won last year's women's competition under their previous name of Northern Superchargers - and have won five in a row going into the final against Rockets, who themselves have triumphed in their last six to clinch top spot in the women's table.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lizelle Lee sent one into the stands as Southern Brave made a strong start

Wong efforts in vain as Brave beaten in eliminator

Earlier, after SunRisers won the toss and elected to bowl first, Lizelle Lee got Brave's innings off to a decent start with a 25-ball 32 that contained five boundaries and a glorious straight six off Kate Cross (1-12) - the only maximum of the match.

The turning point came when Winfield-Hill pulled off an impressive stumping of the South African for the opening breakthrough off the impressive Hannah Baker (2-13).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hannah Baker took two wickets during The Hundred eliminator between Southern Brave and SunRisers Leeds

Baker also accounted for Charli Knott (25 off 21), bowled by the leg-spinner, while Sharma (1-24) went joint-top of the tournament's wicket-taking charts and Sutherland (2-31) snagged a couple late on off consecutive deliveries.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Annabel Sutherland was left agonisingly short of a hat-trick when Dani Gibson's mistimed catch went down, moments after two wickets in two balls

Cross' dismissal of Laura Wolvaardt (8) was the only Brave wicket, along with the run-out of Wong (4) off the last ball, not to fall to spin as Sophie Molineux's side fell some way short of a par score, despite the Australian's 22 not out.

Brave's hugely impressive attack of international bowlers just about kept them in the hunt, Lauren Bell (1-14) conceding just two off her first 10, which included the early wicket of Bryony Smith (2), before Wong cleaned up Litchfield to make it 13-2 after 17 balls.

Sutherland hit a breezy 17 off 12 before perishing to Sarah Glenn (1-25), while Winfield-Hill appeared to be playing a match-winning knock before Wong took two in two to find herself on a hat-trick.

At that stage, SunRisers still required 20 from 22 balls but Sharma and Jess Jonassen (10no off 5) comfortably steered SunRisers to victory and into the women's final.

'SunRisers can't afford those mistakes in final'

Analysis by Sky Sports Cricket's Natalie Germanos:

"A little hiccup from SunRisers at the end - those are mistakes they can't afford in a final, and certainly not against the Trent Rockets.

"They need to be careful in terms of reading the conditions.

"But otherwise, through the day, they didn't get a lot wrong."

Baker: I've never been so nervous in my life!

Meerkat Match Hero Hannah Baker, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I've never been so nervous in my entire life [as during the chase]! It's great to get over the line.

"With our power that we've got, we were always confident that we could chase that. Luckily, we got a bit of spin today.

"I spoke to Jonassen when we were out there and she told me to just hit my length - that's what I did.

"[Now we've just got to] relax, and get ready to go again."

When is The Hundred final?

SunRisers Leeds will face Trent Rockets in the women's final at Lord's on Sunday August 16.

The women's final is at 2.15pm, with the men's final at 6pm, live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Sports.title: RFU postpones start of competitive community rugby season in England
Sports.content:
The RFU has postponed the start of the competitive community game season until the week commencing Monday September 21 due to "concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions".

The RFU had already contacted clubs, schools and colleges, players and coaches to remind them of the existence of guidance surrounding the management of rugby pitches in drought conditions and the Natural Turf Pitches (NTP) Surface Risk Assessment to assess whether a pitch is safe to use and to mitigate the risks of injury.

The prolonged dry weather in many parts of England has left many grounds across the country unsuitable for safe full-contact activity.

After gathering feedback from representatives across different regions and discussing the options within competition committees, the RFU has decided to delay the start of the competitive community game season nationwide.

Sir Bill Beaumont, president of the RFU, said: "We know this decision will be disappointing for the clubs, schools and colleges, players, volunteers and fans looking forward to the start of the season, and we do not underestimate the impact it will have across the game.

"This has been a carefully considered decision. After listening to views from across the community game and weighing up the options available to us, we believe that delaying the start of the competitive season nationwide is the right course of action.

"While we recognise that not everyone will agree with this decision, making it now provides greater certainty for clubs, schools and colleges as they prepare for the months ahead.

"On behalf of everyone at the RFU, I would like to thank all those who have shared their views and contributed to discussions in recent days.

"Player welfare and readiness have been central to our thinking throughout, alongside our desire to give the season the best possible opportunity to begin on a fair and consistent footing across the country.

"We also wanted to provide clarity as early as possible to help the volunteers, staff and organisations who work so hard behind the scenes to plan and prepare for the season."
