Sports.title: Finlay Tarling dead aged 19: British cyclist dies after serious accident during eighth stage of Volta a Portugal
Sports.content:
Finlay Tarling dead aged 19: British cyclist dies after serious accident during eighth stage of Volta a Portugal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

British cyclist Finlay Tarling, 19, has died after a tragic accident during the Volta a Portugal.

The Welsh teenager was riding in the eighth stage of the race when the incident occurred on a 166.8km route to Fafe.

In a statement, NSN said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

'Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

'Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend.'

In a post on X, the Portuguese Cycling Federation spoke of their 'most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones'.

British cyclist Finlay Tarling died in a serious accident during a race in Portugal on Friday

The organisation added that the usual podium ceremony would not take place out of 'respect and mourning'.

Tarling is the younger brother of Josh, a world champion cyclist on the track and stage winner at last year's Giro d'Italia.

Portuguese newspaper RTP reported that the incident had allegedly been caused by a vehicle that did not belong to the race.

The report stated the car had driven on the wrong side of the road and collided with Tarling, who had been behind the peloton.

Tarling was reportedly given immediate medical attention but died shortly after the crash.

Portugal's president Antonio José Seguro said Tarling's death 'saddens the peloton, the race, and the country that welcomed him'.

Seguro offered his 'deepest condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his teammates at NSN Development Team, and to the entire cycling community, joining in their grief with deep emotion.'

A statement from the International Cycling Union read: 'The UCI is deeply saddened by the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling, who passed away following a serious accident during today’s 8th stage of the Volta a Portugal.

'The UCI extends its deepest condolences to Finlay’s family, friends, and teammates.'

More to follow...

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez expected to STAY at Chelsea for the entire season after club's £120m transfer deadline passes with zero bids from Man City and other suitors
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez expected to STAY at Chelsea for the entire season after club's £120m transfer deadline passes with zero bids from Man City and other suitors

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea expect Enzo Fernandez to stay for the entirety of this season after a deadline to trigger his exit for £120million passed without incident on Friday.

Manchester City and other interested parties did not lodge a bid for the Argentina midfielder ahead of the 5pm cut-off, with the Blues insistent that the chances of a departure are all but over.

Fernandez has wanted to link back up with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium, with Chelsea having told the player’s representatives in May that they would facilitate a transfer if a £120m figure was met.

Those terms have now been removed and while City are unlikely to believe a potential deal is dead, they probably would not commit to the sort of outlay Chelsea initially demanded.

City are waiting for Rodri’s future to be finalised, with Barcelona still confident of securing the Spain captain. City want in excess of £60m for the World Cup winner.

The two clubs remain in negotiations over a fee and Rodri – who underwent back surgery after the World Cup - returned to the club’s training ground for pre-season testing on Friday.

Enzo Fernandez is expected to stay at Chelsea for the full season after their self-imposed deadline for clubs to bid for him passed without incident

The 30-year-old travelled back to Manchester on a Ryanair flight to Liverpool on Thursday evening and met Maresca hours later.

Maresca admitted that City still have a significant amount of work to do in the transfer window, with Tijjani Reijnders on his way to Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia for £52m. Tottenham are looking to wrap up a deal for Savinho, with City facing Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday.

Maresca has suggested that there could be further outgoings in the coming weeks.

‘We’ll see what happens with some more, there is a change in this moment,’ the Italian said. ‘We are in a moment where players that were here many years have already left or [others who] probably can leave.

‘And that means there is a change. We're going to try to do our best. At the moment the transfer window closes, we need to be good enough to find as soon as possible solutions for the team.’

The 46-year-old refused to discuss players from other clubs, adding that ‘I don’t think it’s good when people from other clubs speak about our players’ after a summer of discussion around Rodri in Spain.

Reijnders had decided to pursue other opportunities after a lack of starts last season and Maresca believes there are others in the same boat.

‘They all work every day, they all do sessions every day and at the end of the week they all want to play a game,’ he said.

‘When they don’t play, they struggle to understand or they struggle to see the reason why and I can understand that after one season some of them would like to play a little bit more.

‘It’s a bit difficult to convince players when they are already convinced. You need to change their thoughts, that is not always easy.

‘Tijjani’s situation is like James Trafford’s situation and some more players but I think when the club, the player, the manager, they all think the same way, that probably the best decision for a player is to go, you have to go.’

Sports.title: Is Enzo Fernandez really good enough to replace Rodri? And is he worth £120million? Enzo Maresca thinks so - and this is why
Sports.content:
Is Enzo Fernandez really good enough to replace Rodri? And is he worth £120million? Enzo Maresca thinks so - and this is why

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

So, the deadline is set. Friday 5pm. If Enzo Maresca is so keen on his reunion with Enzo Fernandez, he has until then to make his move. Oh, and it’ll be £120million please.

Relations between the two clubs have been better. Maresca resigned as Chelsea manager in January with his heart set on the City job and his former team couldn’t even bring themselves to refer to him by name when they released a scathing statement in June to confirm they had agreed compensation that meant he could replace Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium.

So, what would City get for their £120million if they choose to pay up? Well, what some might call a ‘character’.

One who gets himself sent off in a World Cup final, one who tries to get his Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for Argentina in the same game. One who was frequently booked for dissent throughout the season, one who taunted England fans by cupping his ears after his equaliser in the World Cup semi-final, and one, most damningly, who was accused by his own club-mates of racism after live-streaming himself and team-mates chanting after Argentina won the Copa America two years ago.

Maresca, though, gets a player he trusts more than any other. And if he is to succeed, he will need players he can trust. It said a lot that despite the racism row in 2024, Maresca still handed Fernandez the captain’s armband for the Premier League season opener against City.

Maresca joked recently that Erling Haaland could not possibly be his captain at City because he demands that his skipper race over to him after every goal to receive fresh instructions, unless it was the captain who scored it. Haaland would clearly score too many. At Chelsea, though, even when club captain Reece James was on the pitch, Maresca would often still call Fernandez over once they scored.

So, what would Manchester City get for their £120million if they choose to pay up for Enzo Fernandez? Well, what some might call a ‘character’

This is a player who got himself sent off in a World Cup final. One who tried to get his Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for Argentina in the same game

Fernandez was so often Chelsea’s engine room. Last season, albeit one Maresca left halfway through, the club ranked rock bottom for how far their players ran in the Premier League yet Fernandez sat inside the top 10 for distance covered individually.

Across Maresca’s 18 months at the club, no one played more league matches for Chelsea than Fernandez and only Mo Salah and Bruno Fernandes created more chances from open play across the division.

It looks like Maresca will have to take on the most daunting succession in world football without the most influential midfielder in City’s recent history, Rodri. Barcelona are deep in talks over bringing him back to his homeland.

Without the most reliable metronome in world football, Maresca is going to have to find another way to make City’s midfield tick.

The club have already paid £116million for Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest but he alone isn’t enough. City are also in talks to sign Morocco’s £85million World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi, who is a superb ball-winner and tidy on the ball. Fernandez certainly isn’t a like-for-like replacement.

Both are hugely authoritative and dominant but in different ways. Like Rodri, Fernandez is always at the heart of his team’s attacking play but more frequently at the business end of it.

In his full season under Maresca in 2024-25, he played a part in 200 attacking moves that ended in a Chelsea shot, either taking it himself, creating the chance, or being a part of the build-up. Nearly 60 per cent of them were him having the shot or setting it up. Among midfielders last season, too, he ranked first for expected goals.

By contrast, Rodri’s influence in the previous 2023-24 campaign, the one before he suffered his serious injury, was such that while he topped the list for involvements in his side’s attacking play, only 37 per cent of them were shots or chances he created.

Across Maresca’s 18 months at the club, no one played more league matches for Chelsea than Fernandez and only Mo Salah and Bruno Fernandes created more chances from open play

In Maresca's only full season at Chelsea, Fernandez was involved in attacking play as much as any player bar Cole Palmer

Rodri was also heavily involved in City's offensive work - but earlier on in the build-up

That season, Rodri averaged more than twice as many passes as Fernandez in 2024-25 and at a far higher completion rate with more than three times as many splitting opposition defensive lines.

The Chelsea man, however, was much more direct when he got the ball, playing a higher percentage of his passes forward than Rodri and more of them into the box. Unsurprisingly, Fernandez commits more fouls.

As one colleague who watches Fernandez often put it: ‘Rodri is like the dishwasher, keeps everything nice and clean. Enzo then smashes those dishes.’

One of the biggest differences, and one that Maresca will hope to make the most of, is Fernandez’s superb knack of crashing into the box. Rodri averages less than half a run into the penalty area per game. Fernandez usually makes at least five, and they frequently end up with him scoring.

Like another Chelsea star who made the move to City, he’s Lampard-esque in his ability to find the net following his late runs into the box.

See these examples below, beginning with a trip to Burnley in November, when he bursts forward late as team-mate Marc Guiu charges into the box.

With Burnley’s Josh Cullen (24) distracted by the ball, Fernandez is able to sprint past on his blind side, get to the cutback before him, and strike a first-time shot into the net

Against Brighton, Joao Pedro drops deep to collect the ball, drawing defenders. The ball is played out to Reece James on the right and Fernandez gets on to the end of a cross to head it in

Against Liverpool at the end of the 2024-25 season, Fernandez calls for the ball from Pedro Neto, who cuts it back, by which time Fernandez is there to collect it, take a touch and score

When Rodri was fit and at his peak, Guardiola prefered to use him as a single midfield pivot able to give others like Bernardo Silva the freedom to roam forward, safe in the knowledge that Rodri was there to clean up any mess. When he wasn’t fit, Guardiola would often switch to a two-man midfield.

Maresca has done the same in pre-season with Mateo Kovacic and Tijjani Reijnders there against Atletico Madrid in South Korea. The former sitting, the latter primed to burst forward. It will be interesting to see which of those slots, if any, Anderson takes against Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday.

In terms of style, Fernandez is much more similar to out-of-favour City midfielder Reijnders, who looks set to leave for Saudi side Al Qadsiah. If you compare their heat maps (below), they are both at their most content getting on the ball in the channels.

Rodri proved at the World Cup that he still has what it takes to be the best player on the biggest stage, but so much of the tournament was played at a slower pace due to the heat and altitude in the United States, Canada and Mexico. That allowed him to thrive.

The Premier League is a less forgiving landscape with monsters more effective these days than metronomes.

So, if he is to depart, Maresca seems to have found his way to replace him. It’ll only cost them more than £300million to do it.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta admits he is shocked by this summer's transfer fees - as he opens up on Ethan Nwaneri's future at Arsenal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta said he has been left surprised by the eye-watering transfer fees players have attracted in this window as Arsenal hunt for a marquee attacker.

The likes of Morgan Rogers, who was pursued by the Gunners, have moved on for fees in excess of £100million. The north London club, meanwhile, have been reluctant to pay over the odds for stars.

Bruno Guimaraes was brought in for £75m after a protracted saga, for example. But Arsenal are still assessing the market for forward options, with Galatasaray’s Victor Osimhen and Julian Alvarez linked to the club.

Ahead of Arsenal’s Community Shield match against Manchester City on Sunday, Arteta said: ‘Yes, it has (transfer fees surprised me). I wouldn't bet on that (such high prices) to be fair. But that's the market.

‘There are clubs that are happy to invest or they believe that the valuations of those players are that.

‘And that's fair. At the end the value of the player is what somebody can pay for you and they've done it.’

Mikel Arteta says he has been left surprised by the fees Premier League clubs are spending

He left the door open to Ethan Nwaneri leaving Arsenal if he isn't going to get regular minutes

Arteta also hinted that Ethan Nwaneri could be heading for the exit door.

The 19-year-old sat on the Marseille bench in the second half of last season, and has recently been tracked by multiple clubs, including Galatasaray.

He said: ‘It's unquestionable the talent, the desire, the love and the passion he has for the game. It's something that I've always loved about Ethan. I think he's had some great games and he's shown everybody that he has the ability to be here.

‘I want him to be at the club but something that, in the medium-long term, is best for the player as well. Ethan needs to play football and if he stays here it’s because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes.

‘Otherwise it's just something that is not good for anybody I think.’

Sports.title: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is STRIPPED of Marseille's captaincy for TURNING DOWN £15m Newcastle transfer and 'irritating' club's owner by refusing to leave
Sports.content:
Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has been stripped of the Marseille captaincy after sparking fury at the club for rejecting a £15million move to Newcastle.

The former Tottenham midfielder appeared as though he was closing in on a switch to the Magpies before an abrupt U-turn.

Despite Marseille and Newcastle reaching an agreement for the transfer, Hojbjerg wanted to remain in the south of France.

He's now been stripped of the captaincy, as evidenced by the team sheet for Friday's game against Atletico Madrid.

Hojbjerg was included in the starting line-up but the armband was given to Timothy Weah.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, Marseille owner Frank McCourt is furious with Hojbjerg and the Dane is unlikely to be reinstated as skipper, with reports in France indicating he is still 'irritated'.

Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg sparked fury at Marseille by rejecting the agreed move to Newcastle

Marseille have been under pressure to reduce their wage bill and given their financial difficulties would have welcomed Newcastle's move for the 31-year-old.

But they've been denied that windfall by Hojbjerg changing his mind, putting him in the awkward position of being lambasted despite showing loyalty to the Ligue 1 side.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but he changed his mind over the deal.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Marseille finished fifth after a tumultuous season last term, which included the sacking of Roberto de Zerbi.

Habib Beye replaced him only to leave at the end of the season and Bruno Genesio is now in charge, already having to deal with dressing room unrest.

Meanwhile, it is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, star forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, the manager who saved them from relegation before transforming them into a Champions League club and ending their 56-year major trophy drought, then stepped down on July 31.

They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

Sports.title: Everton transfer briefing: Latest on Iliman Ndiaye and his bumper price tag revealed, why Jack Grealish's return is in doubt, Tim Iroegbunam update, truth about bogus right-back 'targets' and why David Moyes still wants another midfielder
Sports.content:
Say what you will about the Prime Minister but, occasionally, he can make a whole audience nod in agreement. 'Please. Sign a right back,' he said, when asked what he'd wish for his beloved Everton. 'And if we can, get Jack Grealish for at least one more year.'

Evertonians will hope Andy Burnham's lobbying can at least pull some sway with club owners, the Friedkin Group, because, with two weeks of the window left, they are running out of time to fulfil his wishes.

At the end of last season, sections of Everton's support were, somewhat alarmingly, beginning to question whether David Moyes really was the 'Moyes-iah', the manager who could resurrect their club. The team had been transformed from perennial relegation candidates to European contenders ahead of schedule. They were seventh after Christmas. But then they failed to win any of their final seven games and finished 13th and the doomsayers began to spread their gloom.

Short of memory or simply myopic, some raised questions on Moyes' suitability to take the club forward, not recognising that the initial upsurge in form and standards were simply unsustainable on such a small squad.

The Friedkins have not been overly hands-on. They did spend money last summer, not all wisely, but added only Tyrique George on loan in February, days before Grealish was ruled out for the season.

Everton needed that window to have been another building block.

Despite all the progress during his tenure, David Moyes may have to win some Everton fans over after the Toffees' disappointing end to last season

And he might have to do it without Jack Grealish (centre), while Charly Alcaraz (left) and Tim Iroegbunam (right) are both attracting interest

To his credit, Moyes didn't stamp his feet. Nor did he throw underperforming players under the proverbial bus. He appreciated their batteries were simply depleted. But some supporters demand more emotion from him, more anger at their timid finish.

That's not the Moyes of today. Age and experience have honed a more rounded, philosophical coach but any disgruntled fans should not be fooled: this is a man firing on the inside, desperate to mark his second coming with a trophy and more.

But he needs help.

This time out the Friedkins have added Championship Player of the Year Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough for £16.5million. Younger legs compensate for the loss of veteran midfielder Idrissa Gueye. The older head now is 32-year-old Christian Norgaard, an astute £7million addition from Arsenal, keen to make up for a lack of playing time.

Yet they still need greater physical and athletic presence and, with Tim Iroegbunam attracting interest, Moyes would like another for his engine room to support his go-to men James Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. Even though versatile Merlin Rohl has joined on a permanent basis and Harrison Armstrong continues to stake a claim, one bad injury could leave them short.

Iroegbunam's hamstring issue, sustained in a friendly with Stuttgart, has cast his £18million move to Hull City into doubt but is not thought to be serious, and the Tigers are not the only club interested. Fellow midfielder Charly Alcaraz could also return to South America.

Up top, Tyrique George has joined from Chelsea permanently. Everton negotiated a £6million discount on the original option to buy that was agreed with Chelsea. Last week, they got even more creative with a good old-fashioned swap deal, exchanging Dwight McNeil, valued at £20million and with one year left on contract, for Brennan Johnson, valued at £35million and with four years on contract.

On the face of it, Everton have the bargain end of the deal, but Moyes knows that is only if Johnson can find the form of his old Nottingham Forest days and those first season run-outs at Spurs.

Winger Tyrique George has impressed in pre-season after his move from Chelsea

Everton secured a bargain in swapping Dwight McNeil for Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson (pictured) - but Moyes will know he has to help him rediscover his best form

His pace at least will be welcomed. For all Grealish's qualities, he arguably became too predictable: checking, cutting inside, and rarely going outside his full back to cross or shoot.

Similarly, Iliman Ndiaye, another undoubted talent, dropped off in levels after his exertions at the Africa Cup of Nations. Fresh impetus was needed.

Ndiaye has rejected new contract offers but also rebuffed a recent proposal to join Al Hilal. Though no official offer arrived, Everton knew the Saudi Pro League side were capable of hitting the £80million mark that may be enough to buy him.

The 26-year-old wants to stay in the Premier League but he also knows he has admirers at Manchester United, Arsenal and Manchester City. For one reason or another he is not top of their respective lists but that could change if other deals falter.

Everton need workhorse wingers to suit Moyes's style.

They continue to create chances, it's just that in Beto and Thierno Barry they have strikers who too often lack the finish.

Nottingham Forest admire the always willing Beto though and RB Leipzig like Barry. Indeed, when Leipzig's interest in Barry was mentioned early this summer, it was almost celebrated in some quarters.

The ungainly 23-year-old, with three pre-season goals to his name, has vowed to make amends for his debut campaign. He has been studying videos of Didier Drogba, working on his mindset. He wants to change the narrative.

After scoring against Newcastle in Wednesday's 3-1 friendly win, he said: 'I know I can play, now I just need to show it.'

There's no doubt though Moyes would like a more effective striker.

Everton do not have the budget to buy Chelsea's Liam Delap at £55million – but he could yet come into play if no other suitors pounce and a late loan is allowed

A deal for Man United youngster Ethan Wheatley (centre) is more advanced, though Wheatley is one for the future

Talks are coming to a close with Manchester United for Ethan Wheatley but he is one for the future. For the now, the budget is not there to buy Chelsea's Liam Delap at £55million – but he could yet come into play if no other suitors pounce and a late loan is allowed.

Not prolific, Delap is at least disruptive enough to ruffle opposition defences. He is another Forest are keen on and they have the financial clout to buy.

Prior to Chelsea signing Delap from Ipswich, Moyes made a strong impression on the 23-year-old in his pitch to sign him himself.

Everton had only just begun their reformation. But Delap's agents said Moyes was so super-charged in his tub-thumping spiel about why No 9s were revered at his club that they half expected him to rip off his tracksuit and reveal a Marvel Everton superhero suit underneath. Such is his passion to make this work.

The stardust last season of course came from the twinkling toes of Grealish. Many romantics would like to see him return and finish what he started at Hill Dickinson Stadium after injury cut his spell short. Fit and training again after fracturing his foot, Manchester City would be open to a compromise deal with Everton.

A return may suit the marketing department and the owners. There is also little doubt Grealish is a popular figure with all the staff, but in truth, it's a deal that currently has no guarantees of happening.

There's an underlying belief that Grealish's lifestyle away from the training ground, and the circus that sometimes follows, would need to change for everyone to be convinced it was the right thing to do.

In light of that, Everton may give an extended chance for Tyler Dibling to prove himself. There were such high hopes for the former Southampton wing sensation when he joined last summer but the challenge remains for him to convince on the Premier League stage.

Once again, Leipzig are among his admirers and could push to take him before the window closes but Moyes has thrown down the gauntlet for him. Should Everton change tack, then Newcastle's Jacob Murphy is admired.

Tyler Dibling (right) might get the chance to impress after his move from Southampton last year, though Newcastle's Jacob Murphy (left) is admired

Crystal Palace star Daniel Munoz (left) is also of interest, though seen as a right wing-back

Then back to the Prime Minister's wish. A right back.

The list is almost a who's who and Everton may end up by making do.

Budget means they can't afford Newcastle target Amar Dedic at Benfica or Strasbourg's Guela Doue. Kyle Walker is a no, as is Aaron Wan-Bissaka. So is Brooke Norton-Cuffy. Crystal Palace's Daniel Munoz is admired but is viewed as a wing-back, not the orthodox defender the manager requires, so if bought would need them to change style of play. Celtic's Alistair Johnston was on then off but could yet be on again depending on his injuries. The list is being reviewed.

'The profile,' as one agent said... 'is a tall, athletic right back who knows how to defend but can get forward and falls into Everton's budget. But guess what? They're like rocking horse sh**!'

A rarity indeed. But Everton need to find one quick. Then at least the Prime Minister will be happy.

Latest transfer news, rumours and updates as Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Chelsea work to complete deals ahead of the summer window deadline

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives injury update on five Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gives injury update on five Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield

Mikel Arteta was without five key players during pre-season but will able to welcome back three of them for Arsenal's clash with Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday

View 2 Images Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka have returned to Arsenal training (Image: Manuel Velasquez - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka will all be available to face Manchester City in the Community Shield. The Arsenal boss also provided updates on William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, who are both recovering from long-term injuries which they suffered during the World Cup.

‌



All five players didn't feature in any of the Gunners' pre-season friendlies. Rice, Zubimendi and Saka each made it to the final weekend of the tournament with England and Spain respectively, so they were afforded additional time off in order prepare for what's set to be another gruelling campaign at club level.

‌



Saliba, however, went down with a back problem in the opening stages of France's semi-final defeat to Spain. Meanwhile, Timber picked up a serious groin injury just days before the Netherlands kicked off their campaign.

‌



Arteta was asked to provide an update on the quintet during Friday's pre-match conference and had mixed news. "They [Rice, Zubimendi and Saka] will be available. They trained with us today, they will train tomorrow and if they are in the condition that we expect them to be, they will be involved."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Arsenal manager added: "Jurrien is progressing really well, he is on the pitch, we are ramping up now with certain actions and especially the volume and the load. I think he is on a good trajectory, but there is still a few weeks to go. Wilo, as we all know, it's more a long-term injury."

Asked whether Timber could return before the next international break which starts in September and runs into October, Arteta replied: "We have to wait and see. He needs to start to train with the group in the next week or so hopefully, and then see how he progresses from there.

"It's been a long-term issue, and we want to make sure that every step that we take is the right one, he feels right to do that, because he's such an important player for us."

‌



How should Arsenal line up against Manchester City? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images William Saliba's back injury could rule him out for months (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

Both Rice and Saka had fitness issues during the World Cup and had to be managed by England's medical staff. But Arteta hasn't seen anything from the duo that's worried him.

‌



"We haven't noticed anything; they had individual plans through the time that they had with the national team," he explained. "They've been trying to evolve those issues and they have improved.

"In the rest period that they had, they both had specific programmes for themselves. They've been doing those and so far, what I saw the last two or three days, it was really good."

Sports.title: Alice Wood becomes first female Tour of Britain race director
Sports.content:
Alice Wood becomes first female Tour of Britain race director

Having retired from professional cycling in 2024, Wood was announced as race director this March, and she admits her eight-year-old self would hardly believe it.

View Image Alice Wood made history as the first female race director of the Lloyds Tour of Britain Women.

When Alice Wood cycled around MK Bowl at the age of eight, she had no idea she would go on to become a trailblazer in the sport.

‌



Wood, 31, has made history by becoming the first female race director of the Lloyds Tour of Britain Women 2026.

‌



Having retired from professional cycling in 2024, Wood was announced as race director this March, and she admits her eight-year-old self would hardly believe it.

‌



“I think she’d be pretty proud,” said Wood. “When I was riding around MK Bowl, this is something I never would have imagined.

“I started racing nationally when I was eight and internationally when I was 10. It’s been my whole life. I met my husband when I was 14 through cycling, and my sister and I were on the national team together in many World Championships.

“It's something I've grown up with. I love the sport, I still love riding my bike, and this opportunity was the perfect role for me.”

‌



It is a momentous occasion in the history of a race that began in 2014, almost 70 years after the first iteration of the men’s event.

For Wood, her appointment marks both the growing buzz around women’s cycling and a huge personal achievement.

“It means a lot,” she said. “I've loved the thought of event planning, and to be involved in a race like the Tour of Britain is really exciting.

‌



“I'm grateful that British Cycling wanted to bring a female into the role and to be the first to do that is pretty cool.

“Women's cycling is on a real trajectory. We've seen that from the Tour de France Femmes avec Swift and how that is growing year on year.”

Wood will also bring her extensive cycling knowledge to the men’s race, as part of the race unit.

‌



She enjoyed a highly successful cycling career, capped off by 2019 British titles in both the road race and the time-trial.

Despite taking on a different role this time around, Wood is well-informed on the intricacies of the Tour, having competed in the event herself.

Such is her love for the sport, the 31-year-old even trialled Stage Two of the 2026 race - and emphasised the exciting challenge ahead.

‌



“I rode home from the Lancaster Grand Prix a few weeks ago, so I did the two climbs we've got at the start of Stage Two, and they are brutal,” said Wood.

“They're grippy roads and there are some tough gradients, so that is going to be interesting.”

The 2026 Lloyds Tour of Britain begins on 19 August, kicking off on the streets of Cockermouth.

‌



Nineteen teams will take part in Britain’s biggest professional women’s cycling race, with the five stages coming to a dramatic finale in Royal Leamington Spa on 23 August.

“We've got a really strong field, with 13 UCI Women's WorldTour teams and stage winners from the Tour de France Femmes avec Swift,” said Wood.

“I love all of the stages, but I think the finish of Stage Three on the Great Orme is going to be spectacular. It's really exciting.”

Article continues below

British Cycling is inspiring riders and fans across the country through the Lloyds Tour of Britain, bringing the sport to life and celebrating the joy of cycling through Britain's biggest free-to-spectate cycling event. Visit britishcycling.org.uk

Sports.title: As Amy Hunt strives to be fastest woman in the world ex teammate backs her for Olympic gold
Sports.content:
Britain's new golden girl is on a mission to be 'the fastest woman in the world'. Queen of the Track Amy Hunt is not only targeting Olympic Gold but also offering help to the young, gifted and talented.

The new poster girl of UK athletics took centre stage as she clinched a memorable double, winning the 100m and 200m at the European Championships in Birmingham. British Girl Power took the athletics world by storm as Dina Asher-Smith, 30, took bronze and Success Eduan, a 21-year-old midwifery student from Manchester, finished sixth.

Hunt, 24, goes for gold again in the women's 4x100m and mixed relays in a bid to make history as the first woman to win four European golds at a single championship.

NHS admits data breach by sending patient data via pagers READ MORE :

View 6 Images Amy Hunt strikes gold again at Birmingham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



She said: "Two out of four" after crossing the line and revealed that she had overcome low blood pressure which had left her feeling faint in recent 200m races. With 142,000 followers on Instagram, the 'professional fast girl' already has lucrative marketing deals with the likes of Nike and is certain to have sponsors rushing to her door. Her ambition is Olympic Gold.

There has never been a British women’s 100m or 200m Olympic champion in events that have been dominated for almost 50 years by sprinters from the United States and Jamaica. It has been a story of triumph over adversity for Amy.

She overcame an injury crisis in February 2022 when she ruptured the thigh muscle running from the hip to the knee. She moved back into the family home in Newark, Notts., with her devoted parents Claire and Peter. Claire cooked her meals, and helped her in and out of the shower.

View 6 Images Amy Hunt with her women's 200m gold medal (Image: Sean Walsh/Shutterstock)

‌



She says the best part of her success has been paying them back for all the times that they ferried her to early competitions and training. The scar from the injury is a constant reminder of how lucky she is to be fit and competing. She wakes up every day 'thinking about winning Olympic gold'.

The Cambridge graduate combined English literature with sprint and weight training while still at university. A typical day started with Chaucer and ended with a two-hour drive to Loughborough University for gruelling speed work.

She achieved a 2:1 from Corpus Christi College in 2023, despite her injury problems. Afterwards, she vowed to help other young athletes who wanted to be 'an academic badass and a track goddess' like her.

"Life is amazing at the moment, I am just living my dream and I am so grateful to be able to do it," Amy, who is based in Padua, Italy, said. "I am so lucky to live in a different country at 24 and experience all of these things. Loving what I do really comes through. Confidence is such a big part of that. If I am standing on the start line and I do not believe that I can win, then what am I doing there? In every single race, I have to believe that I can do it."

‌



View 6 Images Amy Hunt has a huge social media following (Image: PURESPORT)

She continued: "It is not cocky, but I have to believe in my own success and create a mythology around my own success. It is what you have to do to win. I think for me it was about learning to love the gym a lot more, and I have got to love it now.

"I love going into training every day. I want to be the fastest woman in the world, I want to win Olympic golds and I want to achieve those heights. That is not something I am afraid to say because I am not shy about it and I think it is possible for me."

Amy's close friend Asha Philip, 35, the fellow Team GB sprint star who has just retired from athletics, met Amy and her parents after her 200m triumph on Thursday night and spoke with Amy again today. Asha, a two-time Olympic medallist, told the Mirror: "She was a bit tired and in tears after the race when she saw her mum and dad. She trains abroad so it was a real family moment."

‌



View 6 Images Success Eduan is training to be a midwife while she competes at the top level as an athlete (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

She continued: "A lot of hard work went into those medals as she competed in Glasgow for the Commonwealth Games before Birmingham. She has the attitude that you have to adopt at the very top. We are used to the Americans being very confident and backing themselves.

"Usain Bolt did it and even Mo Farah with the MoBot. But the British generally tend to be more nonchalant. Amy backs herself. I do believe that she can win Olympic Gold."

Asha joked: "I have passed her the relay baton a few times but she is so much taller than me, my face is level with her hand on the changeover.

‌



"I was a mentor when she first came into Team GB and we have stayed close. We have had so many female athletes going through university studies. First Amy at Cambridge, and now Success, who is doing 12 hours shifts as a midwifery student delivering babies. They are superwomen. I applaud them for all the work they have to do to achieve that."

Track legend Sir Brendan Foster, 78, 'loves' the confidence of Hunt and the new generation of female British runners. In the age of Coe, Ovett, Cram and myself, you would tell your coach you were going to win, but you would not say that publicly," he told the Mirror. You would not dare tell anybody else. That has all changed now, there is a change of attitude, and I love it. They not only say they are going to do it, they deliver on the track. That is the Amy Hunt story."

View 6 Images Dina Asha-Smith took bronze in the 200m final (Image: AP Photo/Morgan Harlow)

Mark Brian, Director of Sport at the University of Cambridge Sports Service, was "particularly interested" to hear about Amy's desire to support other athletes studying at Cambridge. "Having successful alumni who have experienced both the challenges of Cambridge and the demands of elite sport can be incredibly valuable for current students," he said.

‌



"Positive role models help demonstrate what is possible and can provide inspiration, practical advice, and mentorship. We would welcome the opportunity to re-engage with Amy and explore how she might support future generations of Cambridge student-athletes in a meaningful way."

Watched by 20,082 fans, the biggest crowd at the European Athletics Championships so far, Amy crossed the 200m finishing line in 22.19 seconds, nine hundredths of a second quicker than Irish silver medallist Rhasidat Adeleke’s new national record and one tenth ahead of Asher-Smith.

Amy, who won the 100m on Monday, yelled “Are you not entertained?” at the camera – a reference to the Russell Crowe epic film Gladiator. Speaking after the race, she said: “It means so much. This year has not been that easy and to do such an iconic thing in Birmingham, as close to my home as I’m ever going to get… To handle all the pressure, to be able to showcase all the work I’ve done, all the work my coaching staff, my family, everything that everyone has put into me – this medal is for everyone.”

Dina said: “I would much rather have had a different colour, but any medal is a medal, isn’t it? I think that’s my ninth European medal in my career. It says a lot to come back year-on-year and perform, and to be one of the fastest women in the world, whatever is going on in your life and still being there, I’m happy with that.” To round off a memorable week for British female athletes, Dina could become the most decorated athlete in European Championships history if she medals in both relays. The current record belongs to Poland’s Irena Szewinska, who won 10 medals between 1966 and 1978.

Sports.title: Arsenal artist leading anti-racism campaign inspired by Bukayo Saka gesture
Sports.content:
Arsenal artist leading anti-racism campaign inspired by Bukayo Saka gesture

Hand of Hope is an anti-racism campaign fronted by world leading artists, one of whom has recreated a powerful image of Bukayo Saka being consoled after the Euro 2020 final

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka was comforted by an England staff member after the heartbreaking Euro 2020 final defeat to Italy (Image: PA)

An anti-racism campaign inspired by a touching gesture caught in the aftermath of England's defeat to Italy at the Euro 2020 is raising funds to fight back against vile abuse.

The campaign, Hand Of Hope, is fronted by world leading artists including Hayden Bone, who has been Arsenal's official club artist for the last five years. Of the 39 pieces of art which is set to go under the hammer, Bone has contributed eight to the collection, including one featuring Bukayo Saka.

The Arsenal star was subjected to horrific racist abuse online after missing a penalty in the shootout that would have seen England land just a second major trophy with victory. Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford were also abused after missing in the shootout.

Saka received a tremendous swell of support following the ugly abuse and the recreation of an image of him being comforted following the shootout will now aid attempts to raise up to £100,000 for causes including anti-racism and the encouragement of youth art worldwide.

Galatasaray reject £111m Victor Osimhen transfer offer as Arsenal task made clear READ MORE :

Bone said: ”I couldn’t be more strongly in support of Bukayo and the defeat of racism. I have painted him many times. He is a kind and thoughtful man who has endured a lot in his short life. He was victimised in an utterly despicable manner, and to come through stronger is a mark of the man. He is exceptional. These paintings are a fitting tribute to him and all the other great athletes who have overcome the sickness of racism.

“Art at this scale will keep the spotlight on the battle against racism. And there’s no better place to start than at school. Kids are blind to differences. If their heroes can inspire them to paint, support a better world, then we can make progress.”

It was a moment in the aftermath of England's penalty shootout defeat to Italy that inspired the collection. Omar Meziane, England's Head Athlete Performance Chef at the time, was seen offering support to Saka by placing his hand on the attacker's shoulder as he digested the events that had just occurred.

View 2 Images

The gesture was snapped by a photographer and quickly went viral around the world.

Meziane, who now holds the same role at Nottingham Forest, added: ”It was a moment frozen in time, a natural reaction. The entire camp had grown very close, which was entirely down to the manager, Gareth Southgate. We really believed we would win. Then the cruellest of endings.

”I saw Bukayo in the moment of despair, alone, utterly crestfallen. He felt my hand on his shoulder, turned to face me, simply nodded in response, no words. His eyes were empty, I knew what was coming, I saw the picture splashed across the media the next day. By then all hell had been unleashed on him.”

The collection of 39 exclusive paintings feature stars from all different sports who have been subjected to racial abuse but fought back. They include Saka, Tiger Woods, Thierry Henry, Serena Williams, Chris Gayle, Vinicius Junior, Neymar and Lewis Hamilton. They all feature in a centrepiece “statement painting” called “Remember Who You Are”.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn's Teramoana Teramoana prediction will become much clearer with next fight
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn's Teramoana Teramoana prediction will become much clearer with next fight

Teramoana Teramoana is being tipped for a title shot within five fights by Eddie Hearn, but he's got to prove himself against a greater calibre of opponent

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn has high hopes for Teremoana Teremoana

The Olympians are coming. Teremoana Teremoana looked spectacular on the Gold Coast this week, making DeAndre Savage his 12th straight victim, all inside two rounds.

‌



The Australian lost to Bakhodir Jalolov in the Paris quarters two years ago, but looks to be adapting to the pro ranks quicker than the double Olympic champion.

‌



Part of that is due to Jalalov contesting two Olympic cycles. Now that his career is being guided by Queensberry Promotions, who have arguably the best crop of heavyweights in the world, the giant Uzbek will be looking to get things moving.

‌



Teremoana is part of rival Matchroom’s stable, which adds to the competitive dynamic and dangles the prospect of a world title rematch between the two Olympians down the line.

Tyson Fury sent clear message as Kristian Prenga sums up Anthony Joshua power READ MORE :

Dana White makes strange excuse for not having ring card girls at Dublin boxing event READ MORE :

Jalolov had just too much experience for Teremoana over three rounds in Paris. That won’t mean much should they meet in the pro ring.

Matchroom chief Eddie Hearn is talking about a world title shot at the back end of next year for Teremoana. That is ambitious even for a ruthless finisher like him. Bigger tests will come but he is certainly exciting. And at 28 looks set to forge a big career.

‌



Teremoana has the power to take out anyone and looks really organised behind the jab. The fundamentals are excellent. I particularly like the way he follows through after landing a big shot. He stays on top of his opponent and throws great combinations.

We have seen excellent Polynesian fighters before but I’m not sure we have witnessed a heavyweight from the south seas as exciting as this. Joseph Parker, a former world champion, of course, has all the tools but never looked as explosive as Teremoana appears.

View 2 Images Teremoana Teremoana produced a statement victory on the Gold Coast

‌



David Tua had a decent career, yet he was eight inches shorter and stocky, the opposite of this guy, who stands 6ft 6ins and weighs 19 stones.

Though there are some terrific athletes from the region, most look to rugby to forge a professional sports career. Teremoana could put a serious dent in that tradition.

I know the importance of rugby in New Zealand, where many of the Polynesian community play, but not even the great All Blacks bank what Teremoana will earn should he go all the way.

Article continues below

It’s still early, of course. The elite guys are not easy to hit, and they can take a shot. Hearn thinks Teramoana is five more fights from a title shot. To make good on that claim Teremoana, like every prospect coming through, must prove himself against opponents good enough to fire back.

Sports.title: Rising golfer, 18, dies after suffering brain haemorrhage before tournament in Thailand
Sports.content:
Rising golfer, 18, dies after suffering brain haemorrhage before tournament in Thailand

Australian golfer Jessica Bang has died at the age of 18 after she collapsed earlier this month while preparing for a tournament in Thailand

View Image Jessica Bang

Australian golf prodigy Jessica Bang has tragically died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage. Bang collapsed on August 1 while visiting Bangkok, Thailand, to compete in the KLPGA Tour‘s International Qualifying Tournament.

‌



She was rushed to hospital for emergency brain surgery, but after nearly two weeks in intensive care, she passed away on Thursday. In a joint statement, Golf Australia and the WPGA Tour of Australasia described Bang as an "outstanding young talent".

‌



The statement read: "The WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community is deeply saddened by the passing of young Tour member Jessica Bang in Thailand.

‌



"Jessica was an outstanding young talent who made a significant impression in her short time on the Tour, winning the Ford Women’s NSW Open Regional Qualifying Event at Moss Vale in February in just her fifth professional start.

"She had earned her place on the WPGA Tour through Qualifying School at the end of 2025, following an outstanding amateur career.

Rory McIlroy U-turns on golf break after pointed message to PGA Tour chiefs READ MORE :

Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"The thoughts and prayers of everyone at the WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community are with Jessica’s family, friends and all those who knew and loved her at this incredibly difficult time."

A GoFundMe was set up by Bang’s cousins to help cover medical costs and organise her return to her family at home. It has so far raised nearly 50,000 Australian dollars (£26,000), but they shared the heartbreaking update on Thursday that she had passed away.

An update posted on the fundraiser by her cousins read: “We would like to thank everyone for your overwhelming support and well-wishes. Sadly, Jessica passed away this morning, August 13, at Synphaet Ramintra Hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, 7.20 am local time.

‌



“As her cousins, we will forever cherish the time and memories we shared with Jessica. Her sense of humour, together with her cheerful and vibrant personality, will always be remembered and treasured by our family.

“The funds we have raised will be given to her parents to help contribute towards her medical expenses. Once again, we would like to express our deepest gratitude to everyone who has supported Jessica and our family through this incredibly difficult time.”

Bang was based in Korea and has family in Sydney and earned status on the Women's PGA Tour of Australasia after winning the prestigious Queensland Amateur last year. In February, she won the Ford Women’s NSW Open Regional Qualifying tournament, shooting a course-record eight-under-par 65 in the final round.

Article continues below

Her round featured eight birdies and an eagle as she won by five strokes. The win was made even more special because her mother acted as her caddie for the competition.

"I'm so happy, I can't even put it into words," Bang said following her victory. "It still doesn't feel real yet. I did not expect this at all - big surprise."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
